notes_for_editor.note: Thin record: NHLR is the only substantive source. The Forest Lookouts Bibb page has a header only (Bibb County, Alabama Forestry Commission) and no body text. The Alabama Forestry Commission Facebook post on fire towers was not readable beyond its title. The 1819 News column is by Thomas Kaufmann, who also nominated Bibb to the Register; it is general about Alabama towers and is cited only for the MC-39 model context, not for Bibb's condition or climbing status. A Jackson's Ramblings entry for Brooks Lookout Tower (Conecuh County) is a different tower and was not linked to Bibb. height_m 30.5 converts NHLR's 100 ft. Access, staffing and current condition are left out of facts because no source supports them. No photos added. Not verified: whether any closure or restoration has happened since 2009.

Build year 1948 agrees across the register, the 1948 newspaper dedication and the blog. Unresolved: the state number is AL 42 in NHLR (and in the record) but AL 43 on Jackson's Ramblings. The register's 100-foot figure is not said to be to the cab floor, so height_m (30.5) is only the register's figure converted and may not match the cab-floor definition. Current condition is not settled: search snippets for a YouTube short and a Facebook reel titled 'Butler Mountain Fire Lookout' describe it as abandoned, but neither page could be read, so that claim is not used. Access, climbing and staffing are unknown; no visit facts are recorded. The record's ownership 'state' is an inference: sources name the Alabama Forestry Commission as administrator, not owner. The 1948 dedication is known only from a newspaper quote on Forest Lookouts; no original newspaper page was read. Verification 2026-10-08: the 428 ft figure is the register's elevation, not a hill height; OpenStreetMap's tag is tower:construction=lattice, not a tower type.

Thin record. The NHLR disagrees with itself: build field 1936, description 1935. No source read gives staffing, closure, fate or current public access, so the story says so. The NHLR links an article, Exploring the Forgotten Fire Towers of Alabama (rootsrated.com), which returned no text from fetch_text; it was not read. A search snippet gives elevation 178 ft (584 m) from aboutus.com, against the NHLR's 563 ft (172 m), which matches the record's 171.6 m; not verified. Access status should be checked with the Talladega National Forest before any visit advice is published.

Two sources only. Build year conflicts: NHLR 1960 vs Anniston Star item (quoted by Forest Lookouts) 1961. The Anniston Star item spells the towerman's name two ways ('Edlers' and 'Elders'); the story uses 'Edlers'. The Forest Lookouts page is a transcription of a newspaper item, not the paper itself. No source read gives the current condition, closure, or access; a search snippet (YouTube) links the tower to Little River Canyon Preserve near Canyon Mouth Park, unverified and not used. Checked NPS pages for Canyon Mouth Park and directions: no mention of the tower. The Alabama state forestry history PDF (forestry.alabama.gov) was searched for Daniel's Gap and had no match in the grep. Check current status with the Alabama Forestry Commission before publishing visit advice.

No source found on staffing history, decommission date, restoration, or current public access/climbability for Parker Springs specifically. The built year (1937) comes from a single hobbyist survey site (Jackson's Ramblings), not an NRHP nomination or Forest Service document; treat it as plausible but not strongly corroborated. height_m (30.5) is a conversion of the 100-ft tower height stated by NHLR, not independently confirmed.

Build date and builder conflict (WPA 1938 vs Alabama Power and CCC, opening April 10, 1939). The Weebly page's Dadeville Record item is dated April 13, 1939 and reports the dedication, so the two April dates are consistent rather than contradictory. Height conflict (82 ft vs about 90 ft) and closure year conflict (1980 vs 1981) are both in the story. Current access rests on CRATA's own pages and a June 2012 reopening note; the sources read do not say whether the cab is open to climbers, so visit.climbable is omitted. Could not read: Roots Rated (0 text returned), Montgomery Advertiser (403), Lake Magazine (429); the LMRA and CRATA restoration-video pages were not read. No photos added; no staffing or last-watch date found.

No source documents staffing history, when fire-watch use ended, or whether the 2013-2016 restoration talk ever resulted in the tower being opened to climbers; current access/climbable status should be verified before publishing a stronger claim. The eastern_us_lookouts cache page (easternuslookouts.weebly.com/wharton.html) was checked but contains only the tower name, county, and preserve name with no additional prose, so it was not cited.

Read: the NHLR page (it includes the 2007 update and the 2019 visit report), Central US Lookouts, the Encyclopedia of Arkansas caption and forest-lookouts entry, and Preserve Arkansas. Open conflicts: cab 12 by 12 ft (register description, Central US Lookouts) vs about 14 by 14 ft (2007 update); single-story base (register description) vs two-story (2007 update). NRHP: the register description says still listed, but the 2007 update says delisted in 2005; the story follows the delisting. The 2000 dismantling date is approximate. No source found for fire-watch years or the last staffing. Access level public is inferred from the absence of any closure, not stated by a source. Current condition rests on the 2019 visit; no newer report found. Living New Deal page returned 403 and was not used.

Current public access is not established by any source read; the story says to check with the City of Hamburg. Living New Deal page returned 403 and was not used. NRHP nomination PDF (Arkansas Preservation) was not reachable. Second search returned no current-status source. The Register credits the Forestry Commission while the handout credits the Aermotor Company and CCC; the story reports both. Wikipedia infobox 1936 conflicts with its text and other sources.

The 1936 build, the land transfers and the 1954 Forest Service transfer come from the register page and agree with the Central US Lookouts summary. Current status is not confirmed: two searches and the register's Arkansas index (which tags it with no status) gave no recent visit or condition report, so the brief's standing was changed to unknown. No source read describes staffing or fire use. The register's cooperator line names the Sylamore Ranger District, which does not fit the St. Francis National Forest description; the description was used and the cooperator line was not. The Encyclopedia of Arkansas media caption for the tower was seen only in search results and was not read or cited. Checker: no source read shows the tower standing today (register page has no visit report); not applied as a status correction because absence of a report is not evidence it is gone. Checker: The story said the Encyclopedia places the tower among the register's Arkansas towers; the entry only lists Horn Lookout Tower in Lee County, so the story now says just that.

The build date is unresolved. The register says the CCC built it in 1938; the Camden News items reproduced on Central US Lookouts (Feb to March 1935) describe the state forestry commission planning and starting a steel tower near Chidester. The 1935 items describe plans, not a finished tower, and no source read reconciles them with 1938. The radio relay use and the 1985 end of service come only from the register page, with no second source. The 1941 survey places the tower about 8 miles north of Camden, while the 1935 notices put Chidester 16 miles west of Camden; these differences were not resolved and the story avoids both distances. An Encyclopedia of Arkansas photo caption (Poison Spring State Park) was seen only in search results and not used. No access information was found, so access is not set.

Build date and design agree across NHLR and the club page. Staffing comes only from newspaper notices copied by the club site (The Baxter Bulletin), so the keeper dates are secondhand and partial. Current access is unknown: no source says whether the tower is open or climbable, so no access key is set. The OpenStreetMap node is not cited in the story. The web search surfaced no independent 2020s source on condition. Suggest checking the Sylamore Ranger District for current status before publishing.

Height conflict left unresolved: 42 ft steel tower (register), 58 ft observation tower (Encyclopedia of Arkansas), 65 ft with a 14 by 14 cab (hiking group page). These may describe different structures or measuring points; not confirmed. Build year: 1952 (register, Encyclopedia) vs 1954 (hiking group page). Elevation: register 2,646 ft (807 m; the record's 806.5 m matches) vs Encyclopedia 2,681 ft. Current hours and climbing rules are not verified; a search snippet describes weekend hours from an older guide and was not used. The Central US Lookouts page was read, but the text returned was only an index, so it is not cited. The record already has a public-domain NARA photo on Wikimedia; no new photos.

The NHLR narrative text says NRHP acceptance was 'October, 1995' while the official NRHP reference number's listing date (via Wikipedia/NRIS) is September 11, 1995; I used the official date and noted the discrepancy. Access status recorded as 'unknown' in facts because sources describe a locked gate on the road but say nothing about whether climbing the tower itself is permitted; did not mark it climbable. Did not use any WebSearch calls; three cached/live page reads (NHLR, Central US Lookouts, Wikipedia) were sufficient. Fact-check (2026-10-04): the summit elevation is also given inconsistently across sources -- NHLR says 1,089 ft, Wikipedia says 1,150 ft; the story follows NHLR since that is the only source the elevation sentence cites, but a human may want to reconcile the two.

Built year 1938 in the brief is confirmed by four sources (NRHP circa 1938, NHLR 1938, Wikipedia about 1938, trip report 1938). The NRHP registration form (received by the state 14 Sept 1993) says the tower was deteriorated at that time; its condition since then comes only from two 2021 NHLR visit reports and a 2020 trip report. No source found the date the tower stopped being staffed, so staffing is dated as of 2021. Access wording needs checking with the Mena Ranger District before publication, since the road-versus-hike conflict is unresolved. The brief's elevation (698.6 m) matches the NHLR's 2,292 ft (699 m). Not read: Living New Deal page (403), ARGenWeb Mena and Oden lookouts page, Grokipedia. Photos not added: the NHLR shows a 1996 photo and a September 2021 photo courtesy Travis Howk, and the trip report shows a 1963 photo courtesy Central US Lookouts, but no image URLs or licences were checked.

Current staffing and public access to the tower itself are unknown. The only staffing evidence is the 2011 register visit report. The Recreation.gov listing is for a separate cabin at the base of the mountain, not the tower, and I did not treat it as tower rental. Two hiker forum threads on hikearizona.com (one saying the tower was staffed, one saying it was padlocked) could not be read (HTTP 403), so they are not used. The 1959 newspaper's 8,000 ft figure is an older press figure and is not reconciled beyond the report and register. No new photos found.

The FS trail page lists the trail under the Payson Ranger District; the NHLR page (and the record) say Pleasant Valley Ranger District. Both are districts of Tonto National Forest; this may reflect a later district reorganization rather than a factual error, but I did not resolve it and left the record's district attribution untouched. Height (~41 ft) and the 'closed to motorized travel' wilderness note come from Mountain Field Guide, a secondary aggregator that cites the Forest Service and Peakbagger; treat with slightly less confidence than the NHLR and USFS primary sources. Climbability of the tower itself (public access to the cab) is not established by any source read; left as unknown.

Build year, height and the cab size agree across the register, Wikipedia and the Kaibab album. Current staffing and any fire history are not documented in what I could read; the register's 'still in active use' has no date. The NRHP nomination PDF on NPGallery (NRIS 87002478) is listed as not yet digitized, so it could not be read. A tourism listing gives the trail as a 4-mile round trip, which conflicts with the Forest Service's 1.3-mile figure; I used the Forest Service page and did not open the listing. Access level 'restricted' is my reading of the sources, not a Forest Service rule. Brief's 'access: unknown' and 'height_m 30.5' are consistent with the sources; no corrections proposed.

Current staffing and whether the lookout is open this season are unknown. The only opening statement is an undated Arizona Highways article. The record's height_m 13.7 (sourced to Wikidata) is not supported by any source I read, so it is not in facts. Summit elevation conflicts: the register gives 9,166 ft (matches the record) while 1935 and 1939 newspapers give 9,264 and 9,242 ft; a paywalled Trails Offroad listing gives 9,227 ft and was not used. The 2014 Forest Service project concerns the summit radio tower, not the lookout. No new photos found.

Build year 1939 agrees across the register and the federal record; Wikipedia's 1933 alternative is noted. Listing date for the NRHP is unsettled (Wikipedia Dec 14, 1987 vs federal record Jan 28, 1988). Rental and staffing status are NOT confirmed. The Arizona Daily Sun article on HistoriCorps restoring the tower to become a rentable cabin returned HTTP 429 on repeated tries and was not read, so no claim rests on it; it is worth a re-read. The Living New Deal page returned 403. The NRHP nomination PDFs on NPGallery are scanned, with no text layer. The Coconino NF cabin pages I read (camping-cabins and Rooms With a View) do not mention Buck Mountain. HistoriCorps Phase I has no date in the sources read. Access and visit are omitted for lack of a source. No corrections proposed; brief's 1939 build is supported.

Height conflict is unresolved: the register says 82 ft, the 1967 Coast and Geodetic Survey description (via Kemnow) says 100 ft. The register also says the tower 'will be transferred' to the register in 2013, which contradicts its own January 31, 2002 registration date; treated as stale text, not used. Present-day status and public access are unknown. The access level 'permission' is my judgment from the reservation location, not a source statement. The 1967 directions may be out of date. Searches for a tribal permit process found nothing. No new photos found. The Fire Lookout Association's managed-unit table, which a search snippet said lists Buckskin as Inactive with a 1963 date, could not be reached in the time budget, so it is not cited.

The history is reasonably documented, but current status and access are unknown. The last staffing found is 1944. The NRHP nomination PDF is not digitized on NPGallery, so its text was not read. The 1913 newspaper item suggests an earlier tower, which the register does not mention; worth checking against Forest Service records. The 50 ft height comes from the lookout history site, not the register. The brief's record had no built date, so events were added. The FFLA rental list and the register's rentals page were checked; neither names Deer Springs. No photos added; licences not checked. Read budget ran about one page over the cap.

Build year 1936 is solid across three sources. Staffing rests only on a 2013 visit report, so current staffing is unknown. Current access, rental and climbability were not found in the pages read. Tower description conflicts: NHLR credits Pacific Coast Steel, while Forest Lookouts gives an MC-24 tower with no maker named. A peakbagging.com search snippet gives 6380 ft; NHLR and Wikipedia give 6157 ft (1,877 m), matching the brief, so the snippet was not used. The Dude Fire burned the Zane Grey cabin, not the lookout; the events list keeps that distinction.

Construction, height, registration and the 1936 groundhouse listing rest on the NHLR entry, with the NPS record matching the 1936 year. Attributing the NPS cabin-and-sheds record to the same groundhouse is an inference, and the story says so. Current staffing, rental and climbing status were not found: a 2017 Cedar City news item and a Kaibab lookout-rental search surfaced in search but the news page returned HTTP 522 and was not quoted, and the search hits did not establish the status. The 2024 Forest Service cabin-rental results concerned other sites. Brief record checked: elevation 2654.8 m, county, agency and the 1996 registration match, so no corrections were needed. The brief has no built-year event; this record adds 1944 and 1936.

Current staffing is unconfirmed; no dated staffing record was found. Access is a judgment: the trail is a public hike, but entry to the cab is not confirmed, so the level is set to restricted. The Pocket Fire fate comes from the USFS page. NHLR gives the Peaks Ranger District, while the 2026 fire page places the fire on the Red Rock Ranger District, so the current district is not settled. The 80-ft wooden height appears only in a search snippet, and the Sedona city and AZ Daily Sun pages failed (403, 429), so no height is recorded. Read budget was exceeded (about 9 page reads) to confirm the 2026 fire fate.

Current staffing is unconfirmed; no dated record after 1950 was read, and the register's 'active service' line dates from its 2001 registration. Access level is restricted by judgment: the trail is public, but entry to the cab is unconfirmed. HikeArizona (403 to fetch_text and WebFetch) has a search snippet saying the tower has been closed to the public since 2009. That is unverified and not used in the story; check it before publishing any access claim. The AZ Daily Sun watchtower story returned 429 and the Forest Service trailhead page does not discuss the tower. Read budget was exceeded (about 11 page attempts).

Status corrected from standing to destroyed. Unresolved: the 54-ft rebuild date (1965 per Forest Lookouts, early 1970s per Peakbagging) and destroyed vs extensive damage in the 2011 fire. Two WMI Central fetches returned HTTP 429 and were not read. A Facebook search snippet says the tower is no longer staffed; not fetched, so not used. Staffing and current access are unknown; no access level is set. The brief lists Escudilla Peak Lookout as another name and says the records share a register number; no fetched page uses that name, and NHLR assigns US 826 to this lookout.

The core history (1936 build, Forest Service ownership, NRHP 1988, NHLR 2001, standing) is consistent across sources. Staffing history, notable fires and current access or rental status are NOT established: the only pages I could read do not cover them, and the NRHP nomination PDF (NARA) and Living New Deal page returned HTTP 403. Search snippets mention summer staffing and a historical-marker text that gives 1906 for the tower, which conflicts with 1936; neither was verified on a fetched page, so neither is used. Do not confuse with the separate 'Grandview' tree lookout (abandoned) listed on firelookout.org at 35.93278, -111.97889. Suggest checking the Tusayan Ranger District for staffing and access before publishing a 'today' section.

Current staffing and any notable fire history are unconfirmed; no source read covers either. Access is a judgment: the road and hike approach are documented, but tower entry is not confirmed, so the level is set to restricted. The 1933 build date and the 54-ft height agree across the register and PeakBagging, but PeakBagging spells the maker Aeromotor where the register says Aermotor. The West Lookouts Greens Peak entry has no event text, only the registry header, so it is not cited. Read budget was exceeded (about 6 page reads plus repeat fetches).

Date conflict unresolved: register and NRHP say 1936; a March 1937 newspaper item says the lookout will be built soon. Design conflict unresolved: NHLR says L-5 groundhouse. A Living New Deal page (HTTP 403 here, so not verified) reportedly says L-4, and the NRHP nomination PDF is scanned with only its cover in the text layer, so its body could not be checked. The westlookouts items are transcriptions of the Prescott Evening Courier, not the paper itself. The 2020 visit report is a volunteer report, not an official inspection.

The register's 2020 visit report (Michael King, October 9, 2020) says 'Staffed? No'. The GrandCanyon.com listing says the tower is generally staffed mid-May to mid-October, which overlaps the visit date, so the seasonal picture is unclear. Height: markers and Wikipedia say 80 ft, the register says 100 ft; brief's 24.7 m is in the corrections list for a human to decide. Builder: CCC versus Kanab contractors is unresolved; the NRHP nomination is a scanned PDF with no text layer on NPGallery, so it could not be read. The climbing claim rests on Wikipedia and a tourism listing; no Forest Service page was read, so the climb is not confirmed by the agency. Brief's elevation 2478 m matches the register.

Build year 1959 and the 54-foot tower with CL-100 cab agree across NHLR and Forest Lookouts. Staffing and access rest on one Forest Service trail page (it carries a July 22, 2025 date line; what that date marks is not stated), which says the tower is used in peak fire season and visitors are welcome; no staff names or fire history found. The brief's access 'unknown' is superseded by the Forest Service statement. No rental listing found; the NHLR rentals page read did not name Juniper Ridge. A Facebook post about the lookout being staffed for the season turned up in search but could not be read, so it is not used. Record height_m 16.5 matches 54 ft. Record lat/lon match NHLR coordinates. No corrections proposed. Climbing status is not stated in any source read, so no climbable flag is recorded.

NHLR and NPS agree on the 1940 date, the CCC build, the 82 ft 6 in height and the inactive status. Access is unknown because no source describes a route, trail or visitor rule. The unstaffed status rests on the 2009 NPS article and NHLR wording, not a current check. The peak-bagging photo is cited only for its date; its license was not checked, so no photo was added to the record.

Current operational status is genuinely disputed between sources: NHLR (page last updated 2016) describes the tower as in active service, and Wikipedia separately attributes a 'open to visitors when staffed in summer' description to the Forest Service -- but checked directly, the USFS Kendrick Mountain Trail #22 page itself says nothing about staffing or visitor access, so that claim should not be cited to the trail page. Wikipedia also says the tower looked damaged and likely abandoned as of mid-2024, with no cited source for that claim. Worth a human check (e.g. a recent trip report or current USFS fire lookout roster) before updating the tower's staffing/access fields. The tower record's 'kind' field (two_story) comes from FFLA's '2-Story Cab' classification, which doesn't obviously match NHLR's description of a flat-roof cab on a 10 ft tower -- plausibly just differing naming conventions rather than a real conflict, so no correction proposed, but flagging it.

Good primary-register coverage (NHLR + NRHP nomination metadata + FFLA list), but nothing on named lookouts, specific fires, visitor access, or current staffing/climbability turned up in cache or the three web searches used. The elevation figure conflicts between NHLR (8,467 ft) and the NRHP record (8,250 ft) and should be looked at by someone who can check the actual nomination PDF or a topo map. Height is also given two ways (48 ft vs 49 ft) by the two registers. No cached page existed for this specific lookout outside nhlr/ and ffla/; fflos (abandoned-sites register) has no AZ Lake Mountain entry, consistent with it still standing and in service.

Dates and location agree across NHLR, NRHP and Forest Lookouts: 1928 replacement on Lemmon Rock, 1988 NRHP listing, 1997 NHLR registration, June 2015 closure to visitors. The current status is not confirmed: the latest notice read is the 2015 closure and no reopening was found. Design is thin: the sources read say only lookout house, building, architect unknown; a search snippet from the GVRHC Lemmon Rock PDF describes a ground-mounted L-4 structure, but that page was not read because the page-read budget was spent (not used in the story). The NRHP nomination PDF returned HTTP 403 and an Arizona Daily Star article returned HTTP 429, so neither was read. Wikidata lists elevation 8,773 ft against NHLR 8,720 ft (2,658 m); the record's 2657.9 m matches NHLR, so NHLR is followed. A Historical Marker Database snippet calls it the oldest lookout still in use on the Forest; not used because the page was not read. Record kind 'ground' is consistent with the NRHP building record but no source read states it in those words. Record access 'unknown' should now read closed (2015 notice), not confirmed for today.

Current staffing/access status is only as current as these pages (dates on them unclear), so the tower record's staffing/access fields are left 'unknown' rather than overwritten; story says staffed 'each fire season' per source wording. No photos beyond the one already in the tower record were found within budget.

The 1956 claim about a forest fire is cited to Wikipedia only; the reference Wikipedia cites was not opened. The newest staffing evidence is the 2013 GVRHC summary; check the current season status before trusting it. Access 'public' means trail access on foot, not a cab tour; no source states a cab-entry rule. The NHLR and GVRHC agree on the 1916, 1922 and 1966 towers.

The build dates (1936 original, 1983 replacement) and the 2002 registration come from the NHLR detail page only. Standing status comes from the firelookout.org listing. The date the 1936 tower reached the museum is unknown, so no relocation event is set (events need a year). The NHLR museum page URL the record links as '../us-az-mount-ord-at-rim-country-museum/' returned 404, and the Go-Arizona and Payson Roundup pages returned 403 and 429, so the museum's account (whole tower or only the top section) is unresolved. Search snippets (not used) mention a 2013 forum thread about decommissioning and a rotating camera; they were not verified on a fetched page. Access and staffing are unknown. Suggest checking with the Rim Country Museum (Payson) or the Tonto National Forest Mesa Ranger District before publishing a 'today' section.

History from 1911 to 1976 comes from newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; those items were not checked against the original papers. The NHLR page is the only source for current status ('remains in active service', undated). Access level is not stated in any source read, so access is omitted; the record's access 'unknown' stays. No trail or visit information found. The Forest Lookouts page has a 1996 'National Register' entry whose text was cut short in the page output, so it is not used. Height 30 ft converted to 9.1 m. Record elevation_m 2419.5 matches NHLR 2,420 m. Record tower kind matches the NHLR description. No corrections proposed. Search results and listing sites about current access were not read, so nothing from them is used. The Forest Service Bradshaw Ranger District page was not read.

Height 22.9 m is converted from the register's 75 ft; the brief had no height. Elevation in the brief (2793.5 m) matches the register's 9,165 ft; Dangerous Roads gives 9,179 ft (2,798 m) and was not used. The April 25, 2009 registration date and the July 4, 2009 ceremony are both recorded; they are not in conflict. Staffing is not stated in the fetched pages. Public access status is not confirmed; the only road detail comes from a travel guide. The Abbey claim rests on the travel guide alone. The Forest Lookouts North Rim page gave no tower detail in the text fetched. The 'summit' location comes from the travel guide only.

Current staffing and climbing status are not established by any source read; the story says so. The 1959 history comes from a compiled newspaper log on westlookouts.weebly.com; the original clippings were not checked. The brief's access 'unknown' is changed to restricted based on an undated Forest Service alert. The 1952 memo and 1959 newspaper quotes are secondhand via that compilation.

Current access and rental status are not established by any source read; the only visit report on the register is from 2010. The record's point (34.36717, -111.01275) is about 1.4 km from the register's coordinates (N 34.377000, W 111.022250); not changed, a human should check which is right. The 1913 to 1952 history comes through newspaper quotations collected on the Forest Lookouts page, not the original newspapers. The LS-40 model name appears only on the Forest Lookouts page. The NRHP nomination PDF did not come through as readable text, so the nomination itself was not used. Height correction is proposed, not applied. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the first-tower sentence now cites both sources, and the 1921 to 1925 sentences are reworded to the sources. A March 1914 Albuquerque Herald item also credits C.H. Kissam, deputy forest supervisor, with building a 100-foot tower in the Sitgreaves forest; the story gives the credit to the 1921 Winslow Mail report and does not reconcile the two. The tower record at data/towers/az/us-az-promontory.json still shows height_m 35.1; the correction in this file's corrections array has not been applied there, so a human should decide it.

Thin record. The NRHP nomination PDF on NPGallery is marked not yet digitized, so the 1939 significant year and any staffing, use or closure history could not be checked. Staffing and rental status are not found in any source read; NHLR page shows no visit reports. Not read: Living New Deal (403), Heritage Index (403), Grokipedia (not used; unreliable mirror). The brief's 2452.1 m elevation matches the NHLR's 8,045 ft (2,452 m). The brief's NRHP number 87002451 is confirmed by NPGallery. The NHLR's 'MC-39' model differs from another mirror's 'MC-40', which was not used. No photos added. Worth a second pass against the digitized nomination if it appears on NPGallery later, or from the Forest Service Alpine Ranger District.

No build year is given beyond the Forest Service's early 1980s, so no built event is recorded. The 1913 plan is a newspaper report of a plan, not confirmation that a tower was built. The access level 'restricted' is our judgment from the trail being open and the lookout being an active staffed lookout; no source says whether the cab is open to visitors, so change it if the Tusayan Ranger District says otherwise. Record name, coordinates and elevation match the register. The Forest Lookouts page also carries a 1972 newspaper report of a violent death at the lookout shack; not used, because it concerns private individuals and says nothing about the lookout itself. The Wikipedia article repeats the register's design text and is not cited. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the earlier draft's sentence that an earlier structure may have stood on the butte but the sources describe none is removed, because a 1972 item on the Forest Lookouts page calls a 'Forest Service fire lookout shack on Red Butte', which predates the early-1980s tower. The story now says only that the sources do not say when a tower first went up. The 1972 item is not used in the story, and its crime report is not used at all; an editor may add the shack, without that detail, if wanted. The directions now name Forest Roads 320, 340 and 340A, as the Forest Service trail page gives them from Tusayan; the earlier draft named only 340A.

The azrock.org 2022 post was read but not used: it calls the tower wood and stone and no longer in use and gives a 7,255 ft peak, both at odds with the other sources. Current staffing rests on an undated blog and an undated Forest Service page, so a dated source would strengthen it. Flickr photos (alanenglish) turned up in search but were not read or added. The CCC attribution comes only from the blog.

Brief's record (1935 built, NHLR 2004 registration, NPS agency, unknown access) checks out. Access can move from unknown to public for the hiking trail, but whether visitors may enter the cabin is not documented. Sources disagree on build details (stone base in the register vs frame on masonry in the narrative) and the narrative also has a 'by 1937' summary that is compatible with the 1935 finish but less precise. Summit elevation (NPS 7,310 ft) differs from the register's lookout elevation (7,238 ft). No specific fire at the lookout was found. The 2008 NRHP date is Wikidata-only. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list shows coordinates 32.01414, -109.32508, slightly off the register's 32.01111, -109.32639.

Nearly all of the history rests on one register entry, plus Wikidata for the county. No newspaper, Forest Service or tribal source was found, and the latest staffing date is 2011. Access is listed as unknown: the story says no public visitor information was found, and it does not infer permission rules. Photo candidates not added: a 2008 Panoramio photo on Wikidata (license not checked) and the register's 2008 photo credited to Chris English (license not stated). Three web searches were run for this lookout, one over the two-search budget.

Closed status rests on the register's wording ('closed to public access'); the register page carries no date, so current status should be confirmed with the Kaibab National Forest Williams Ranger District or the Army before the access note is trusted. The NRHP listing 87002481 is titled 'Volunteer Lookout Cabin' and is a building with significant year 1939; whether it refers to the tower, the earlier wooden lookout or another structure is not stated in the sources read. The record does not show the NRHP listing; a human should decide whether to add it. The 1921 newspaper items name the trail builder H.S. Perry; no further detail was pursued. Record height 9.1 m matches the register's 30 ft; coordinates and elevation match the register. Flickr and tripbucket search snippets repeat the register's closed-access wording; they were not read and are not cited. No photos added. Fact-check 2026-10-08: 'contractor' is replaced with 'successful bidder' (the Williams News wording). The Volunteer Mountain location now cites the Forest Lookouts page too, and the 1930s start-date sentence cites both sources. The 1988 listing is confirmed by NPGallery's date-published field (1/28/1988).

Tower fate is disputed. The Weebly page says it was destroyed; the 2020 NHLR visit and the GVRHC hiking-club report both describe a standing steel frame. The story reports the dispute. Height: the record gives 13.7 m, but both the register and the hiking club give 46 feet (about 14.0 m); a correction is proposed. Model (MC-40 vs CL 100-106) and elevation (9,984 vs 10,029 ft) are unresolved and both are reported. The Living New Deal page and the NARA nomination PDF returned 403, so the NRHP nomination text itself was not read; the CCC architect claim comes from the NPGallery record. Staffing and the trail note are from the May 2020 register visit only, not checked since. The GVRHC PDF publisher name is taken from the domain and was not confirmed from the document. Read budget: seven read attempts, one over the six-read cap (two of the attempts were 403 errors).

Thin record. No visit report, staffing record or fire history was available: the register page has no visit section, and the FFLA list gives only the status 'Standing'. The NRHP nomination text could not be read (NARA PDF returned 403). Search snippets of the nomination, which I could not quote, give conflicting figures: about 45 ft Aermotor HC-40 with a 7 ft cab in one, and 99 ft Aermotor nC-40 with a 7 ft cab in another. Both differ from the register's 46 ft LX-25; this is unresolved and the story uses the register's figure. The proposed height correction (13.7 m to 14.0 m) assumes the register's 46 feet is the right figure. Leads not read: a Western News article of 2025-09-05 about volunteer restoration of historic Arizona lookouts (may cover this tower); a 1964 newspaper item describing a three-person fire-watch crew (historic staffing, snippet only). The Living New Deal page returned 403 and the weebly page for West Peak returned 404. Read budget: six reads, all used.

Brief record checks out: 1936 build, 2001 NHLR registration, USFS agency, 46 ft (14.0 m) height. The NRHP nomination PDF itself was unavailable (HTTP 403 on the NARA S3 copy), so the design and NRHP details rest on the NPGallery metadata, Wikidata and the NHLR page. Staffing status is not given by any source read; the only staffing evidence is the 1912 timeline entry. A Facebook group post says the tower has not been regularly staffed for some time, but it is undated and was not used. Living New Deal also credits the CCC with the 1936 build; not fetched. Access is unknown; the brief's unknown stands. Sources differ on the tree-stand start (register 1910, timeline 1912 stationing) but they are not contradictory. Photos on Wikidata (Woody Mountain Lookout Tower (full).jpg) have no fetched URL and were not added. The 1936 current-tower date is inferred from the register's wood-tower span ending 1936 'when the current tower was built', not from a stated build field. The timeline has no entries after 1936.

Brief height_m 24.4 is 80 feet; corrected to 18.3 m (60 feet) per NHLR and HistoriCorps. Elevation differs: NHLR 6,192 ft, HistoriCorps and Campflare 6,225 ft; not in facts or story. The closed-to-public status rests on an undated third-party Campflare listing that cites no Forest Service page; check the Eldorado National Forest before relying on it. The Eldorado cabins page grep found no Alder Ridge mention. A 2000 news item on the Forest Lookouts page reports a death at the lookout; it is left out of the story as not needed for the history. No source read gives staffing or fire history, and no source confirms a rental has opened. No photos added.

Brief's record checks out on 1966 build, NHLR US 1147 / CA 112, San Mateo County, and standing status (FLA). Brief's 'They share a register number' conflict: Wood Butte, Oregon is listed in the FFLOS register as US 1147 (OR 495) in data/towers/or/us-or-wood-butte.json, while Allen is NHLR US 1147 (CA 112). These are different registers, so the numbers may just coincide; I did not verify this against a single register. Brief's coordinates (37.38709, -122.29501) match the FFLA list, not the NHLR point. Register text gives the tower height as '51" 6" high', which is probably 51 ft 6 in; I did not add height_m because the reading is uncertain. Register says it was closed in 1981, which I recorded as staffing 'unstaffed' as of 1981; the register does not use the word 'staffed'. Access is unknown; the register is silent on visiting. Register photos are credited to Scott McClintock; no image URL was captured, so no photos were added. The register's Salinas origin is not confirmed by the other sources read. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story's 'dry spell' wording was replaced with the source's 'unseasonably dry weather', and the 1956 item is now footnoted in the story.

Build date conflicts: NHLR says 1914 (first service); the plaque says the original lookout was built in 1924 and the current structure by the CCC in 1935. The story reports both. Registry conflict, not in the story: the firelookout.org California list (https://firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/) gives NHLR US 1180, CA 115 at 38.88230, -120.05465, while NHLR's own page gives US 518, CA 56. The brief's number matches NHLR and was kept. No source read describes the buildings after the June 2010 photo captions, so the current condition is unknown; closed/standing rests on NHLR's undated description. Access is inferred from the Forest Service road page, which does not say whether the buildings are open. No photos added: the Weebly captions cite a July 1941 National Archives photo and June 2010 photos by Ron Kemnow, but give no image URLs. OpenStreetMap way 905267264 (Angora Fire Lookout, tower:type observation) was checked but not used. Budget: 9 distinct pages read against a 6-page budget (the CEQAnet and Forest Service pages were needed for the fire date and access), plus 2 web searches.

Access level and climbability are not stated by any source read, so the access and visit keys are left out. The FFLA California list at firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/ codes the lookout as a 2-Story Cab, Standing, NHLR US 182, CA 7, which matches the record's kind and the register. The record's $500 figure comes from cr-rest-2020.pdf, not the cr-ca-north-2020 report, which gives no amount. The 2021 staffed mark is five years old. A WebSearch turned up a trail-guide snippet saying the modern lookout is manned during fire season, but that page was not read, so it is not cited.

Two substantive sources agree on the 1993 restoration, 1994 registration and the 1990 condemnation; they disagree on build year (1932 vs 1934). The 2026 staffing claim comes from a single article (kymkemp.com) that appears to repost a Forest Service item; treat as seasonal staffing as reported. Sources read do not say whether the public may visit or climb the tower; rental status not found. The Register visit report from 2007 records staffed yes but was not cited. Elevation in a peakbagging entry (6,960 ft) differs from the Register's 6,891 ft; the Register figure is used. Height 8.8 m in our record is unsupported; see corrections. No photos added.

Distance from Quincy is disputed: the register's 2005 visit says 6 miles east, a 1937 Plumas Independent item says about 12 miles east. Not resolved; the story reports both. The record's 'built 1934' is the register's construction-start date; the newspapers show the permanent station completed in November 1937. A human should decide whether the built field needs a correction. The register's 11' figure is not labelled (cab, tower or height), so no height_m is given. The record's event 2025 'restored' overstates the FFLA report, which lists the work as ongoing; it is recorded here as 'other'. The FFLA California list at firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/ agrees with the register: Encl. Tower, Standing, NHLR US 601, CA 72.Access level is not stated by any source read, and the last register visit is from 2005, so access and climbability are left out. Staffing 'unstaffed' rests on the 2005 register visit, which is old. The 1994 notice names the Quincy/Greenville Ranger District; the register now names the Mt. Hough Ranger District.

The name in the record, Babbit Peak Lookout, matches the register, so no name correction is proposed; the 1929 and 1965 items use Babbit and the 1930 to 1960 items use Babbitt. The record has no built year; the 1929 newspapers support 1929 as the build year (construction was announced for July 1929 and the building was in use by late August). That is recorded as an event, not a correction. The 1928 and 1929 papers place the station on Bald Mountain. Identity with the register's Babbit Peak is inferred, not stated, and should get a human look. The newest staffing record is the 2011 register visit; the 2007 and 2009 FFLA reports describe staffed use but not current status. A web search turned up a 2025 Sierraville Ranger District page that does not mention Babbitt Peak; search snippets were not read, so nothing from them is cited. The FFLA list agrees with the record: Encl. Tower, Standing, NHLR US 515, CA 53. Access level is not stated in any source read; left out. No new photos were added.

Construction dates conflict for the first structure (1942 vs about 1943) and the current tower is 1950 in most sources. Status data is thin: the fire-lookouts.org page was last updated in 2013 and Peakbagging.com's closure date (1986) has no other source. No source read gives a current visitor policy for the cab. Elevations differ by about 260 ft depending on whether the lookout or the summit is meant. Fire-lookouts.org credits its cost and historic-eligibility points to a 1988 report that was not read directly. Trail length conflicts: CalWild gives 2-3 miles round trip; fire-lookouts.org gives two miles from the parking area to the lookout (about four miles round trip). The story gives both.

Thin record: the NHLR detail page is the only substantive source. Its build, cab, transfer, administration, staffing and registration facts all come from that one page. The Forest Lookouts Butte County listing has only a February 23, 1929 quote about a planned 60-foot steel tower on Baldy Peak, east of Stirling City; it does not name Bald Mountain. The tower record data/towers/ca/us-ca-bald-mountain-cal-fire-butte-county.json has height_m 18.3, which equals 60 feet and so may have come from the Baldy Peak quote. No source read gives this lookout's height, so height_m is left out of facts and story. Please confirm or remove height_m in that tower record. Checked 2026-10-08: the register footer (raw crawl cache) reads "Last updated on July 31, 2020", which dates the page, not the staffing note. Not in facts or story: a search snippet for the Butte County Battalion 1 page (buttecounty.ca.gov/553/Battalion-1) says the lookout is no longer staffed by lookout personnel and has two ALERTCalifornia cameras. That page returns HTTP 403 to both fetch_text and WebFetch, so it is not footnoted, and the snippet is not quoted. A human should check it, because it would change the staffing and today sections. The transfer to CDF is dated only to the late 1950s, so no event year is given. Staffing has no as_of date: the register footer says the page was last updated July 31, 2020, but our reader drops that footer, so it is not cited. Access, climbability and current condition are unknown and left out. No fire history was found in the sources read. Searches returned other Bald Mountains (Maine, Idaho, Inyo, Mono, Sierra, Sequoia and El Dorado National Forests), which were excluded. No photos added; the record's three NHLR photos are all-rights-reserved.

Do not confuse with us-ca-bald-mountain-sierra-nf (a different lookout in Sierra NF). The record's '2024 assessed' event (site visit on 24 May) is not in any page read, so it is left out. The record's access value 'unknown' is replaced with public, based on the Forest Service road page and the FFLA visitor count. The 1956 and 1969 items come from newspaper quotes reproduced on the weebly page, not from the newspapers themselves. The FFLA testimonials on the host page are dated September 2026, which hints at 2026 staffing, but no 2026 report was read, so staffing is dated 2025. The 1980s end of full-time service has no exact year in the sources, so it has no dated event. The PDF calls the lookout '61-year-old'; that is not used.

Do NOT use the 2025 'Visiting Volunteers' end-of-season report (firelookout.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/cr-cal-s-bm-2025.pdf), the 2026 Record-Courier article, or firelookouthost.org/bald-mountain: they concern a different Bald Mountain lookout on the Inyo NF (Mono County, built 1963). Build year is unresolved: register 1954, fire-lookouts.org and a 1955 Region 5 memo point to 1955; the story says so. Road date is unresolved (register: about a decade after 1954; fire-lookouts.org: 1967). The record's 2004 'restored' event (propane lighting, lightning protection repair, potable water, benches) was not found in any page read and is left out of the story; please verify or drop. The record's 1999 and 2001 registration events are both kept; the event notes explain the difference. height_m 12.2 converts the register's 40-foot tower; it is not stated whether that height runs to the cab floor. The cr-az-2009.pdf file is a multi-chapter FFLA compilation (first section is Arizona); the Bald Mountain passages are in its California sections, and one of them says Sierra National Forest where every other source says Sequoia. Staffing is 'seasonal' from the Forest Service page (manned, summer hours). The same PDF's 2009 Sequoia status list says Bald Mt was 'Staffed 5 days with USFS GS employee', which conflicts with the volunteer 'not staffed' entries; the story reports both and does not resolve it. The fire-lookouts.org page was last updated in 2013 and its staffing line is dated. No new photos added. Budget used: 6 distinct pages and 1 web search.

Built year conflicts: the register gives 1934 for a 20 ft tower, California Lookouts gives 1936 for a CCC-built 18 ft 6 in tower; both kept in the story, not resolved. Record height_m 10.0 looks wrong. Nothing after the 2008 photos describes the cab, and no current access notice was found; status 'standing' rests only on the FFLA list. Newspaper quotes come through a hobbyist transcription page, not the originals. Do not confuse with the Inyo NF Bald Mountain Lookout in Mono County (1963 tower), which search results return first.

The 1916-1923 staffing/construction detail comes from an enthusiast compilation site (californialookouts.weebly.com) that cites period Siskiyou County newspapers and a 1952 USC&GS data sheet; I could not verify those primary sources directly, only the compiler's summary of them, so treat names/dates in events for 1916-1923 as secondhand. The NHLR-dated 1938 tower and the 1919 lookout house are almost certainly two different structures on the same peak (record's 'built: 1938' event refers only to the surviving tower) - worth a note on the tower page if the editor wants to preserve both construction dates. Several undated NHLR photos (a 'California Plan 4A Cabin' and a 'Tree Platform') suggest yet other structures/eras on this site that no source dates; not added as events since no year is given. Kathy Shoopman's start-year lookout is called 'Bald Mountain Lookout' in the Action News Now piece but multiple other outlets (ABC10, Yahoo/AP, KTVL) place her first post at 'Baldy Mountain Lookout... west of Happy Camp', matching this record; I treated it as the same site given the matching location description, but flagging the name discrepancy. No source found addresses current public access, trail, or drive-up status, so visit/access facts were left out rather than guessed.

Brief height_m 18.3 matches 60 feet (NHLR). Brief built 1927 is stated as circa 1927 in NHLR; no correction proposed. Elevation 1,035 m (NHLR) matches the brief. Access moved from unknown to restricted per NHLR (undated quote from a 1991 visit, MVT 10/91, and the 2019 register text). No source read gives current staffing, current fire-detection use, or a 2020s visit. A June 2024 lightning fire that damaged transmitters on Bear Mountain appears in search results (KMPH, Fresno Bee, Newscast Studio) but the Fresno Bee page timed out and was not read, so it is left out; worth checking. Forest Lookouts and the 2007 report disagree on the house's fate only through the Register. The area is 'Squaw Valley' in these sources; a later name change was seen only in an unreliable mirror and was not verified. No photos added; the Register's 1955 Cal Fire photos have no image URLs in the text read.

Access is marked restricted, not unknown as in the brief, because the sources describe a working fire site with no public visiting arrangement; treat that as an inference. Staffing as_of is undated (USFS brochure). The 1916 and 1994 items are Mountain Democrat notices as reproduced on the californialookouts page, not the newspaper itself. Brief's 'events' correction: the 1935 original build was missing. The USFS PDF has interleaved columns and ligatures; quotes were copied from extracted text and need the ligature in 'staﬀed' to match. Lead not used: californialookouts also quotes a Sacramento Union item of September 15, 1911 that calls it the Big Hill lookout, so staffing may go back before 1916; the story's 'at least to 1916' remains true.

No staffing history (first/last staffed, notable fires) found in the sources checked; story says so plainly rather than guessing. Minor built-year (1934 vs 1935) and tower-height (10' vs 11') discrepancies between NHLR's narrative and structured fields/Recreation.gov are noted but not fully resolved.

The sbnfa.com page in the brief returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The current-conditions 'Closed for the season' line on the Forest Service page was read on 2026-10-08 and may not reflect a later reopening. NHLR's undated 'seven days a week' staffing claim conflicts with the Forest Service's fire-season hours. The NHLR description says the cab was restored after the 1980s but gives no year, so no restoration event is recorded. A photo log (peakbagging.com, May 2022) gives a 14 ft cab on a 20 ft steel tower; that was not used because it is a single hobbyist source that conflicts with the NHLR cab dimensions, which were not quoted in the story. The 1928 and 1929 Rita Morris items are secondhand quotations on a lookout history site; the originals were not checked. No notable fires were found in the sources.

Status is standing per the 2017 register text and the May 2025 hike report, which describes it as dilapidated and not safe to climb. No source found a fire at the lookout. Last staffing year not found; newspaper items run to 1946. Elevation differs across sources (7,765 / 7,769 / 7,792 ft); register figure matches the record. The 1933 newspaper item also reports a personal arrest of the previous lookout; left out of the story. Built year 1935 comes from the register alone; no construction record found. Access is hike-only in wilderness; no current closure notice found. Do not encourage climbing.

The Register's 'still staffed each year' wording is repeated by dangerousroads.org, so it is not independent confirmation; the Register's own visit reports point the other way. No 2025 or 2026 source on current staffing or access was found. The summit road description comes from a road-trip site, not a land manager. A Scott Valley News Facebook post about the tower was not readable (login wall). A SummitPost entry for a Blue Ridge in Tulare County (1930, 60 ft) is a different tower and was not used. Our record's height 33.5 m matches the 1952 survey, not the Register's 80 ft. No photos added; the Register page carries captions only, with no image URLs.

Built 1934 from the register; a 1924 newspaper item already refers to a Bonanza King lookout station, so an earlier structure may have existed; not resolved. Access conflict: the 2009 register visit says 2WD for most of the road, while the Dangerous Roads guide says 4WD required and a closure October 30 to May 1 (undated third-party guide). Elevation 6,956 ft (register) vs 6,955 ft (1987 article and guide). The record's kind 'ground' fits the cab-on-foundation description. A Trinity Journal column reporting an AlertCalifornia wildfire camera at the lookout turned up in search but could not be fetched (HTTP 429); not used, worth a recheck for current status. The 1929 lookout injury and death is kept unnamed in the story. Current staffing status after 2009 not confirmed.

Core history (1948 tower, 1983 end of service, 2011-12 restoration, 2012 reopening, FFLA staffing from 2012) is supported by two or more sources. The 1921/1934 earlier towers rest on NHLR, FFLA, SDUT 2012 and Friends. The brief's events not verified here and left out of the story: the 2010 agreement with State Parks, the 2016 'opens' item (the NHLR link title only), the 2017 mast and leak work, the 2019 FFLA $300 grant, and the 2023 $300 door-frame grant. The 2023 year-end report confirms the mast repairs and structural funds but not the $300 grant. A 2017 Voice of San Diego search snippet (not read) gives 'Built in 1946'; this conflicts with NHLR and FFLA's 1948 and is noted only here. The SDUT 2012 photo-gallery URL in the brief returns 404. height_m is converted from 30 ft.

Access is private land per the Register; the story does not describe any route and advises staying off private land. Height 9.1 m is the 30 foot tower height from the Register description; it is not a total height. The Register's 2019 registration and 2012 trip report agree the tower stood then; the 2025 post reports a threat from the Gifford Fire without saying whether the structure survived, so current condition is unknown. Staffing: last staffed 1992 per logbook; a landowner's account in the trip report is not repeated. The FFLA post is Facebook; its text was read through the post page, not a login. No photos added: the NHLR photos are credited to individuals and USFS, and no image URLs were read.

Standing lookout; the record's 1942 build date matches the NHLR and fire-lookouts.org for the present cab, so no correction is proposed. Sources disagree on the cab style (L-4 vs C-3), the wooden tower dates (1930/1931/1938) and elevation (7,386 vs 7,548 vs about 8,000 ft). The staffed and open-to-public status comes from a page last updated 2013; NHLR says in active service but gives no date. No 2026 confirmation was found. The weebly page has the 1928-1935 newspaper items. The Living New Deal page returned 403, so it was not read. Story is about 365 words including footnotes.

Thin record. The register (1979) and the 2008 FFLA Western Region report (a brand new lookout completed and opened on Brush Mt.) disagree on the build date, and the report does not say whether it replaced an earlier cab. Left unresolved, so not in resolved_conflicts. The North Coast Journal feature is undated in the cached copy and contradicts itself on staffing (fully staffed June to mid-October versus staffed only in extreme fire danger). Staffing is recorded in facts as disputed, not resolved. The access level public rests on that feature alone; worth confirming with the Six Rivers National Forest. Record elevation 1226.2 m matches the register. Not used: a peakbagging.com search snippet giving 3,988 ft (not read). Not checked: Six Rivers NF pages and any recent closure notices. No new photos. Elevation figures disagree slightly between sources (8,408 ft brief/NHLR vs 8,502 ft fire-lookouts.org); story avoids stating a number. Did not verify current 2026 staffing status beyond fire-lookouts.org's general description of the season-staffed, public-access model, which is longstanding but not dated to this year specifically.

Rental status unconfirmed: Campflare shows the site as Closed and says a 2025 rental was anticipated but not on Recreation.gov; a Roamze listing repeats the 2025 expectation. Did not verify the brief's 2017 $500 FFLA grant; the 2018 report mentions only the 2016 grant to this site. The 2016 grant amount is not stated in sources read. Two WebSearch calls used (budget met). A lookout station was staffed in 1932, before the stone tower's 1942 build year in the record; the story presents the station and the tower as separate stages.

Build year 1935 is supported by the Register Built field and the 1935 newspaper reports; the Register's 1933 CCC claim is the only dissent and is reported in the story. The brief's access was 'unknown' and is now public with a seasonal schedule. The 2025 season is the latest confirmed opening; 2026 status is unverified. Elevation is given three ways (8,419 / 8,502 / 8,535 ft) and the story shows all three. The 1970 Bear Fire spotting comes only from the Mountains Foundation page; no separate fire record was read. Checked 2026-10-08: the 8,502-foot passage is from the October 31, 1935 report; the 'so no tower' link is now attributed to the peak's elevation. The telephone and road line now says what the report says (a link to the Green Valley-Fawnskin truck trail). The Register's 2026 90th anniversary does not match a 1935 build year (1935 + 90 = 2025), so it may count from completion; the story reports the Register's wording without reconciling it.

Record's 'design' and 'height_m' fields are still null; NHLR only confirms it is an enclosed tower cab (matched by FFLA's 'Encl. Tower'), not a specific design code (e.g. L-4) or structure height. Current access level for visitors (open vs restricted) isn't stated by either source beyond the gated BLM road detail, so access.level is left unknown rather than guessed. Fact-check 2026-10-04: the original draft claimed Cahto Peak's own FFLOS registry number was 'US 2049, CA 155' — on the FFLOS list that number actually belongs to the adjacent, unrelated, 'Gone' listing for Cahoon Rock; Cahto Peak's own FFLOS row instead cross-references the NHLR number (US 1125, CA 110). Story and this evidence entry were corrected to drop the misattributed FFLOS number.

Build year is disputed: NHLR says 1942, Peakbagging's June 2010 note says 1944. Staffing and condition come from the November 2019 NHLR visit report; no newer report was read, so present-day status is unconfirmed. The 30-foot tower height is from Peakbagging and converted to 9.1 m. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced with restricted, based on the 2019 report's locked gate and permission-only private road. The 1945 Gates death is implied by 'overtaken by fire' rather than stated outright; the story says only that he was overtaken. The Lessons page misspells the lookout as 'Casandra'; that spelling is not used. The firelookouthost southern-california table lists Calandra near the word 'Operational', but the text was not clear enough to cite, so it is not used.

Elevation differs slightly between the brief (1778.8 m / 5,836 ft) and Recreation.gov (5,980 ft) — not flagged as a correction since it's a minor discrepancy in secondary description text, but worth a glance if precision matters. Did not independently re-verify 2004 NHLR registration date beyond the brief. Verification pass 2026-10-04: removed the story's claim that the enclosed windmill-style design was 'common to CCC-era towers in California' -- neither source supports that; Recreation.gov instead says only three examples of this style survive, which argues the opposite of 'common.'

Two distinct prior structures are easy to conflate: (1) a 1924 lookout on Bear Basin Butte itself, burned 1936, unrelated to the current building; (2) the Camp Six/Upper Coon Mountain cabin (built 1934 per NHLR, or first built 1923 per FFLOS with an undated later replacement cabin) that was moved to Bear Basin Butte in 1996 (recreation.gov) or 1997 (FFLOS) and is the structure standing today. The tower record's own 'built: 1934' event matches NHLR but not FFLOS; left as-is since it's directly sourced. No corrections proposed to the tower record itself -- its fields (name, location, status 'relocated', agency) all check out against these sources. The FFLA CA list entry confirms 'Relocated' status and the NHLR US 288/CA 21 numbers; an adjacent table row for a different lookout (Basalt Hill, NHLR US 880/CA 90) sits right next to this one in the cached HTML and could be misread as a conflicting register number for Bear Basin Butte -- it is not, it belongs to the preceding row.

Well sourced on history (newspaper run in the Forest Lookouts page, register visit report, 2025 chapter report, park guide). Points to check: (1) Demolition is reported second-hand by the FFLA California-South 2025 report from park correspondence dated 12/12/24; not confirmed with Pinnacles National Park. Worth a call before publishing the status note. (2) Elevation: the record's 949.8 m is the register's lookout figure (3,116 ft). Parkwolf and Wikidata give the summit of North Chalone Peak as 3,304 ft, so the two may describe different points; not reconciled, not used in the story. (3) Cost figures differ: 2018 stabilization $200,000 (register) and $300,000 to $1 million to restore (2025 report); the story says they may cover different work. (4) The 1935 station and the 1951 destroyed lookout are not confirmed as the same structure. (5) The 1951 cause differs between the 1951 report (butane from a refrigerator or stove) and the 1952 report (gas from a tank lit by a refrigerator pilot light); both are cited. Record kind enclosed_tower and height 6.1 m are consistent with the register's 20 ft steel tower. Access level closed reflects the boarded door and the unestablished public access, not a closure order. No new photos added. Budget: NHLR, Forest Lookouts page, Wikidata, Cal-South southern page, Parkwolf (moved page), plus the 2025 report; one search.

Construction date conflict (1924 NHLR vs 1929 Wikipedia) is unresolved; the brief's 1924 is kept with a note. Height 7.3 m is the Wikipedia infobox total, not the 12-ft tower. Staffing as_of is inferred from the chapter home page saying six years since the 2019 restoration; the page has no explicit date. Access marked restricted is an inference from the volunteer-run working lookout. No public visiting info found; current status in 2026 unverified beyond the chapter site.

Sources are thin. The NHLR is the main source; the Forest Lookouts page supplies the 1990 budget-cut note; Peakbagging.com has a 2006 photo caption; the Bay Area Peaks trip report is undated. The Forest Lookouts page also lists 1931-1938 items about Signal Ridge and a Greenwood lookout, and a 1956 Ground Observer Corps entry that does not clearly name this site; none of these were used. The ffla-ccwr.org page in the brief could not be fetched (name resolution failed), so it was not read. No current owner or access policy was found. No source read places the station on the summit, so the story does not say so.

The Forest Service page (updated August 31, 2026) lists the site as closed after the Timber and Plaskett Fires and says it is reachable only on foot; the story says so and does not encourage a visit. The record's 'all-metal tower' design conflicts with the register and Forest Lookouts descriptions of a wooden ground cab later sided in metal; it is kept in facts.design and the record's design field is not on the corrections list, so please decide whether to change it. status stays 'standing' in the record; the status_note is a judgement call (standing, but full of radio gear and not in use as a lookout) and can be dropped. Staffing 'unstaffed as of 2023' rests on the 2023 year-end report and the 1990 last-staffed date. The 2024 and 2025 Cal-South annual reports (cr-cal-south-2024.pdf, cr-cal-south-2025.pdf) show the same repeater-gear wording in search snippets but were not read, because of the page budget. A 2025 report snippet (cr-cal-s-m-2025.pdf) says there is no current direction to move the repeater equipment out of the lookout; also unread. The FFLA Monterey page gives its location as '60 miles southeast of Monterey', which looks wrong, so it is not used. Historical cab and roof facts are from the register and Forest Lookouts page; the 1923 build year is consistent across both. No new photos. Budget used: 6 distinct pages and 2 web searches.

The build history rests on the register alone: 1931 for the first lookout on a water tank, 1938 for the present K-brace tower. No second source explains the sequence. The record's Wikidata value (1938) is noted only. Access and the hiking-only route come from SummitPost, a climbing guide, so treat them as secondary; the register does not describe public access. No NRHP listing, staffing record or visit report was found, so the staffing status is unknown. The FFLA list gives only 'Standing'. The 2020 SCU Lightning Complex coverage found in search concerns Lick Observatory and is not about this lookout, so it is left out. Access level 'permission' is my reading of the SummitPost advice; the register does not state a permit rule. Read budget: three page reads; the cached FFLA and Wikipedia-list pages were checked locally.

The brief's 1931 build and 1998 NHLR registration are confirmed. NRHP listing (1996) and the 1995 nomination were not in the brief's events and are added. The Wikipedia 'still in use in the 1980s' is a decade, not a year, so no year-specific event was created. Staffing as_of is the 1995 nomination date, the only staffing detail found. The Atlas Obscura and Parkwolf listings were seen only in search results and are not cited.

Build year conflicts (1932 steel tower per fire-lookouts.org vs 1934 CCC tower per NHLR); both are reported. The brief's L-4 design is only the 1932 cab; current cab is C-3(L). The brief's NHLR registration date (2019-12-23) does not appear in the cached register text, so no nhlr_registered event was added. A Deadwood Lookout Rec Cabin in Idaho (destinationwild.com) is a different tower and was excluded. The EverybodyWiki article is flagged as AI-generated and was not used. Significant three-way disagreement on the current tower's height/origin/install year across all three sources used; flagged in both the story and resolved_conflicts rather than silently picking one. Brief's access was 'public'; narrowed to 'restricted' with a note since sources say it's only open to the public when staffed (intermittently, via volunteers). Did not independently verify the Buck Rock Foundation's current program status beyond what fire-lookouts.org states. The 1930 two-room house and 1943 telephone-line rebuild sentences were confirmed live on californialookouts.weebly.com but had no evidence entry in this file; added 1930/1943 events and folded their quotes into the existing cite-3 evidence entry.

The build date is the main open question: NHLR says 1935, and newspapers describe 1938-40 construction. The record's height_m of 23.0 is not supported by any source read, so it was left out of facts. The record's kind three_story conflicts with the NHLR's two-story tower. A 1950 Daily Independent Journal item in the Forest Lookouts list reports a dedication on June 8, 1950, probably a retrospective column; unresolved and not used. The record's 1974 build date and elevation (NHLR 7,145 ft = 2,178 m; record 2177.8 m) match the NHLR, so no correction is proposed. Sources disagree on the history between 1948 and 1974 (1949 opening vs 1948 erection vs 1952 dedication vs a 1979 replacement of a WWII airport control tower), and the story says so. The CAL FIRE PDF is an undated copy hosted on a personal site. The Lassen Historical Society item on susanvillestuff.com returned 403 and was not read. Story is about 380 words including footnotes.

History is well sourced from four pages. Current status is not: the latest staffing source is 2010 and no access rules were found, so no access or visit facts are recorded. The register gives elevation 6,483 ft while the Jenner blog gives 6,444 ft; neither is recorded in facts. The brief's conflict note says the record shares a register number with another entry; I did not check that other entry, and US 104 is what the register page shows.
