The ODNR tower page (ohiodnr.gov .../armintrout-fire-tower) returned 404 in the cache, and the current visiting rule rests on a 2016 article plus an undated CompassOhio guide, so access should be checked. Original height conflicts (80 ft in the panels, 71 ft in OCJ). The 1934 newspaper items spell the family name Armentrout; the NHLR and panels use Armintrout. The panels and OCJ describe the fairgrounds as the Ohio State Fairgrounds, not the Ohio Exposition Center named in the brief. No notable fire is named in any source read. The Weebly newspaper items come through a lookout-history site, not the newspaper itself.

The ohiodnr.gov pages for this tower returned HTTP 404 when fetched, so the state's own page is unverified. The register and both guides agree on 1934 and 80 feet. The restoration has no date. The cab-access point comes from a visitor comment on the register page, not from the owner. No staffing history or notable fire was found. The record's agency (Ohio Department of Natural Resources) is unchanged; the register names the Ohio Division of Forestry as cooperator.

Access and current condition are not confirmed. The ODNR pages for this tower returned 404 when fetched, so their claims about climbing and CCC construction are not quoted or relied on; verify them before publishing. Height 30.5 m is taken from the 100-foot figure in the 1938 item. No named fires found. Record rests on NHLR plus two secondary lists.

Core history is consistent across the NHLR, Portsmouth, Scioto Historical and 1924-1948 clippings: built 1924, first fire tower in Ohio, 60-foot steel. The restoration has no date in any source read; 'recently restored' appears on pages that are themselves undated (Scioto Historical photos from 2011-2013; Portsmouth post dated 2022-02-04). The NHLR visit report (2003) is the only condition report and predates the restoration. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced with public, climbable at own risk. The ODNR Copperhead page returned 404 to both fetch_text and WebFetch, so ODNR's own visit details are unchecked. The Scioto Historical URL is the mail. subdomain as cached. The date the tower stopped being staffed is not in any source. Staffing 'unstaffed' rests on the NHLR 'Staffed?' field alone.

Height is disputed between sources: NHLR's register entry (recorded 2014, pre-move) gives 45 feet; the Metro Parks blog (post-move, more detailed) gives 82 feet to the cab floor; Columbus Navigator says 100 feet overall. I used 82 ft (25.0 m) in facts.height_m as the most detailed account, and flagged the discrepancy in the story rather than silently picking one. The destination record us-oh-keystone-at-scioto-grove-metro-park may want the same height note and a built-1942 event added; not edited here since this task scoped only us-oh-keystone. Fact-check 2026-10-04: Columbus Navigator also attributes the donation to 'an anonymous private landowner', conflicting with the Metro Parks blog's naming of the Taylor family; the story follows the Metro Parks account only, which the evidence supports, but a human may want to reconcile this.

The original ODNR page returned HTTP 404; the Ashland Source reprint of the ODNR story was used instead. The 1978 closure date is statewide, not a Mohican-specific date, and no source gives the year Mohican itself was last manned. The marker photo credit (Craig Doda, 2025) was not added because no license was shown. The register's 125-foot figure is the only outlier.

Built year, height and restoration year all conflict across sources. The HAER record at loc.gov (oh1794) returned HTTP 403 and was not read; it is the likeliest tie-breaker for the build year. The Ohio Exploration Society text places telephone service at the cabin in 1935, which conflicts with its own 1939 build year, so that line was not used. The register's graffiti comment is undated. The staircase removal rests only on Abandoned Online. The Forest Service order is the current authority: it closes the tower and was last updated June 10, 2025.

The tower's location after the city's purchase is unconfirmed. The Sandite Pride item does not name the tower but its details match Beaver's (100 feet, from Cookson, on the register); a human should check this with Sand Springs Parks or the Oklahoma Forestry Services. The News On 6 story is dated October 8, 2019 on the cached page. The register does not place the stump near the summit, so the story omits that detail. The Sandite Pride item's date is not printed; its URL suggests March 2020. Because the date and move are uncertain, no event was recorded for either. The record's status 'standing' may be out of date. The 1960 staffing comes from one newspaper quote. Height 30.5 m is the NHLR's 100 feet. The SummitPost access note is undated.

Two independent, consistent sources cover the build/rebuild history well (1926 original, 1937 rebuild, 1974 storm loss and Aermotor replacement with the footings-error deck), but neither says anything about staffing history, specific fires spotted, or current public access — those fields stay unknown. Flagged a height correction: the record's 30.5 m (100 ft) reflects the tower's planned height, not the 75 ft (22.9 m) it was actually built to after the footings error; worth a human call on which figure the map should show. Did not refetch nhlr.org or firetower.org per the guide; no additional web search was needed given the two cached sources agreed.

Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): the draft had the tower 'watching over the surrounding Ouachita National Forest' and being in active service 'as of' its 1997 register listing, both attributed to NHLR. Neither is in the NHLR text — the page only says the tower 'is still in active service' as of its last update (Nov 2016), with no statement about what it watches over or forest-boundary claims. Softened both in the story and removed the unsupported forest-duty claim. Also split the 1974 storm-destruction citation to NHLR only, since the Forestry Service page never mentions a storm. Rewrote the Aermotor-rebuild paragraph, which had tracked the NHLR sentence structure too closely (same clause order and several repeated phrases like 'measuring error at the footings').

No access level or visit rules were found, so access is left out of facts. The NHLR's 'remains in service' has no date and is the only current-status source. The 2018 press release is the latest visit evidence. LASR (403) and a Facebook post (login wall) could not be read. The height correction (16.8 m to 30.5 m) is the main change to the record; check the 100-ft figure against the tower if measured data exists. Staffing today was not found.
Brief's 1964 built date and R-6 design matched all three sources exactly; no corrections needed.

Built-year conflict (1942 vs 1943) unresolved; story notes both. Fact-check 2026-10-04: re-fetched the NPGallery asset record directly; it has no explicit 'listing date' field, but gives Date Published 12/29/2000, so the nrhp_listed event year was corrected from a placeholder 2003 to 2000. The story itself states no year for the NRHP listing, so no story edit was needed there. All four footnoted citations and their quoted evidence were spot-checked against the live sources and confirmed verbatim.

Brief record: design L-4 describes the 1934 cab, not the standing 1960 cab; correction proposed. Staffing is disputed across three sources (NHLR: ODF; firelookout.com undated: Ochoco NF; Aug 2023 Malheur NF notice: BLM). Access is provisional: the 2023 notice is the only source on visitor access and says nothing about entering the cab. Search results also included a different Aldrich Butte in Washington, near North Bonneville; it was not used. No photos were added: the NHLR and firelookout.com photo credits have no licence or URL in what was read.

The build year is disputed (1928/1929/1930) and the register's 1963 is unsupported; the story says so. The 1974 move is well documented by a contract quoted on Forest Lookouts. The record's coordinates match the register; another source in the brief's record gives a point about 470 m away, which was not read. Whether the cab is open to visitors inside is not stated in any source read. The 2022 Cheryl Hill visit is the newest source. The register's 1963 may be a data-entry error; a Malheur NF or NHLR contact could confirm.
No staffing dates or named lookouts found; built year (1931) is consistent across NHLR and firelookout.com. No contradictory info encountered for this tower.

Status is disputed and needs a human decision before the record changes. The FFLA Oregon 2007 report lists Bald Butte as lost in 2007 and burnt to the ground; the May 2018 visit describes the tower as still standing, abandoned and in bad shape; firelookout.com (undated) says condemned and severely vandalized. The record's 'standing' is left unchanged. Height: record 2.4 m is wrong; the register and Forest Lookouts say 41 feet, so a correction to 12.5 m is proposed. The first tower's height also disagrees (register 45 ft pole tower; 1931 Ochoconian quote 42 ft wood tower). Staffing: register says 'staffed as needed' (undated); 2018 visit says not staffed in decades. Elevation: record 1788.3 m matches the register's 5,867 ft; firelookout.com gives 5,920 ft, not reconciled. Forest designation: the register and Forest Lookouts say Ochoco National Forest; the coordinates are in Harney County, which I did not check against forest boundaries. Sources are thin and two are undated blog or personal pages. Page reads used: 7 (one over the 6 guideline, within the 8 cap). No WebSearch used.

Brief's location conflict (NHLR vs RIDB coordinates) was not resolved here since it doesn't affect the narrative; recreation.gov currently lists amenities as unavailable due to vandalism/storm damage, worth double-checking closer to the 2026 rental season for accuracy.

Record height 18.3 m appears to come from the 60-foot tower announced in 1928, not the present 29.5-foot tower; correction proposed. The 1928 tower's height and the first-lookout date are disputed in the sources. Staffing is contested (firelookout.com says staffed; a Cheryl Hill index says unmanned) and undated; check with Walker FPA or Fremont-Winema NF. Cheryl Hill's index also gives 1947 in the same row; that is not used. The register's 'Fremont National Forest' is now the Fremont-Winema NF. Access (whether the cab is open to visitors) is not stated in any source read. The 2003 registration date is from the register. A May 1941 newspaper item names a builder for the new tower; the register says the Forest Service constructed it, and the story follows the register.

Sources conflict on the 1933/1934 tower (10 vs 20 ft), the present tower height (50 vs 54 ft 6 in), and current status (register says active service; firelookout.com says emergencies only). Staffing as_of is undated. Elevation: record 793.1 m matches the register's 2,602 ft; Cheryl Hill lists 2,866 ft. Access is set to restricted from the Cheryl Hill column; confirm with the Douglas FPA before any visit advice.

Access 'permission' is inferred from Weyerhaeuser land ownership and the 1965 permit; no current access rule was found, and the story gives no visiting directions. The 2025 visit report calls the cabin abandoned and barely standing and describes a bushwhack, so the record's status keeps 'standing' with a status note. The 2025 report lists a 20-ft steel tower, which conflicts with the cabin in other sources; check the type before using 'design'. A 1935 US Forest Service recovery note places the station at the center of the lookout house but gives no size. The 1953 Coast and Geodetic Survey note may describe an earlier house rather than the 1949 cabin. The record's elevation (1677.3 m) follows the NHLR figure.

Access 'restricted' is inferred from firelookout.com's 'available for emergencies' (undated); no 2020s source confirms current use. The 2010 peakbagging photo caption (dated July 16, 2010) says the lookout was staffed by two people; the names are left out of the story. Elevation was not reconciled: NHLR gives 2,172 m (matches the record), firelookout.com gives 7120 ft, peakbagging gives 7126 ft. The record's height_m of 3.0 m is only the 10-ft base; check it before publishing a height. The 1975 and 1962 items come from newspaper excerpts on the Forest Lookouts page, not the newspapers themselves.

Sources disagree on the builder (register: Santiam Lumber Company; the August 1950 item quoted by Forest Lookouts: Fire Patrol crew) and on distance from Sweet Home (32 miles in the August 1950 item, 16 miles on firelookout.com); the story reports both without choosing. The record's '2007 restored' looks wrong and is proposed as a correction; the 2007 report describes a survey and winter sealing only. Design labels differ (BC-301, L-4, 14x14 type). The original cab burned to the ground on June 21, 1951 (Albany Democrat-Herald, quoted by Forest Lookouts); Every Lookout in Oregon says it was reconstructed in 1951. The sources do not say how much of the standing cab is the 1951 rebuild, so the 1950 build date may not describe the structure visitors see today. An earlier note that no notable fire appears in the sources was wrong. The 2020 Holiday Farm Fire came close; the lookout survived. Access: private timber land behind a closed locked gate; a gate sign allows non-motorized recreation at fire precaution level 1 or lower. The 2026 description is a single blog visit.

Brief record errors: height_m 3.0 and design D-6 describe the cupola and the wrong structure; corrections proposed. The 1934 tower dimensions, collapse date and cupola date conflict across sources. Current staffing is only confirmed to 2019 (Nugget) and July 2016 (Cheryl Hill). No current access source was read beyond the 2016 blog, so the public-access level is provisional. Oregon.com, Oregon Hiking and Hikespeak showed up in search results and were not read; one gives 62 ft for the replacement, which is not used. The NHLR photos (1972 DNF archive; 2006 Ron Kemnow) have no URLs or licences, so none were added.

Only three sources. The NHLR and firelookout.com pages are both undated, so current status and staffing are unverified. Build year conflicts (1936 NHLR, 1933 firelookout.com). Brief design L-4 and height 6.1 m match the NHLR's 20-ft pole tower; the 20-ft figure is read as the tower height. Searches mostly returned the Black Butte near Sisters (Deschutes NF, Jefferson County, 1934/1995 towers) and a 2021 Black Butte Fire 8 miles NE of Antelope Lookout; neither is this tower and neither was used. Access is provisional. Editor should check with the Prairie City Ranger District on current status before publishing. No photos added.

Current status conflicts: the register describes the Douglas association staffing it, while firelookout.com says emergency status and the 2015 visit found it not regularly staffed and boarded up. The 1996 vs 1997 remount date is unresolved. Elevation: record 784.6 m matches the register's 2,574 ft; firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill give 2,696 ft. Record height 6.1 m vs present 20 ft 4 in (6.2 m) is a small difference, so no correction is proposed. Staffing as_of is undated. Visit route comes from a 2015 blog visit; recheck before publishing any visit advice.
NHLR's 'legs later removed... low stone base' and 'recently restored... catwalk' changes carry no specific dates. The Slater Fire's exact burn date isn't pinned down beyond 'September 2020'.

The 1961 build date and the 2022 registration in the brief check out, and no corrections are needed. The 1920s cupola and 1930s wood tower have decade-only dates, so they have no event years. Access level is left unset because no source describes current public access or rental; the brief's access 'unknown' still stands. The 2016 'abandoned' label conflicts with the registry's emergency-use note; the record follows the newer source. Sources are hobbyist lookout sites plus NHLR and the Forest Service repeater project; no construction contract or agency history was found, so the reason for each replacement is unknown.

Height 9.1 m is the 30-foot tower, not the elevation (brief's 1968.7 m is elevation). Unresolved: timber (NHLR, firelookout.com) vs steel (Peakbagging) for the 1980-81 tower. Newest condition evidence is a July 2, 2017 photo; no later source checked. No rental found. The lessons.wildfire.gov page covers the same 1979 fire (a 20-person crew deployed shelters) but does not name this lookout; it marks its date approximate and was not used for crew details. Brief's 1981 build year is kept. Access set to private from the NHLR 'Private Land' field and Peakbagging.

Record says 1952 built; the register says Relocated 1952 with unknown original construction date (correction proposed). Status is standing as a physical cab but abandoned as a lookout (facts.status). Elevation: 1,628 m on the register matches the record; feet differ (5,341 ft register, 5,331 ft firelookout.com and Every Lookout in Oregon, 5,333 ft in a 2017 hiking blog not used as a source). Staffing list from firelookout.com names individuals; the story omits names. Access: the cab is reached from a roadside overlook on National Forest land; the 2022 register notes (open door, glass on floor) are the only interior condition record, and the story does not advise on entering. No notable fire, no rental and no restoration appear in the sources reviewed. Confidence high on the 1952 move; the parking and road access rest on a 2023 visit account.

The brief's 1996 build date is right for the current steel tower; the first lookout on this site was a 1937 cab on a water tank, removed in 1965. Access is set to restricted from a 2021 visit report and the compound layout. No official current visitor policy was found, so this should be checked with the association. The elevation conflict (77 m vs 240 ft) is left open. No photos added.

Design labels conflict and are not resolved: D-5 ground house (Forest Lookouts, Every Lookout in Oregon), Region-5 cab (firelookout.com), 14x14 'Supervisor Hall Special' on a revised California design (register). The register page dates from the 1994 registration and describes the ground cab as the lookout, which predates the 2001 tower. Elevation: register 6,666 ft (record's 2,031.8 m matches), firelookout.com and Every Lookout in Oregon 6,695 ft. Staffing 'every summer' on firelookout.com is undated; the dated record is the July 2021 visit. No rental listing found in the FFLA rentals page or the sources read. Access: a rough forest road to an active Forest Service lookout; no visitor rules in sources, so access level is public with a check-first note. Record kind 'tower' and height 15.2 m match the 2001 tower, so no correction proposed. Story edit 2026-10-08: the 1927 cab's presence on the summit is cited to firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts and Every Lookout, not to the register, which does not date its cab; the staffing sentence is limited to what the sources date.

The brief's height_m of 4.9 is not supported by any page read, so it is left out of facts; please verify or drop it. Staffing claims come from undated firelookout.com text plus a June 2022 trip report, so the as_of date is the research date. The 1920 and 1930 construction dates conflict in the register and are reconciled in the story. The 2022 trip report is a personal blog and is used only for road and visit conditions. Current 2025-26 staffing was not checked. The 1920 report's 14x20 two-room house and firelookout.com's 14x20 guard cabin (1922) may be the same building; the story reports both as sourced and does not say they differ.

The record's ground kind is supported by Cherylhill's L-4 Ground Cabin, though the NHLR's with-catwalk wording suggests a raised cab; the record was left as it was. Build year and elevation conflicts are reported in the story and resolved_conflicts. The Forest Service page is the current source for staffing and rental status. No photos added.

Staffing: Cherylhill's June 2022 visit and the July 2026 directory both say unmanned. One undated search snippet (peakbagging.com) says it is staffed in fire season; I did not read that page, so it is not used. Access is set to public because the directory counts the site as legally accessible; the story tells readers to view the tower from the road because it now holds equipment. The 1935 tower and the 1949 vs 1951 move are left as conflicts for the editor. No photos added.

Heights conflict: the 1934 tower is 35 ft (Forest Lookouts) vs 30 ft (firelookout.com and the register); the present tower is 41 ft (firelookout.com) vs 44 ft (register). Staffing as_of 2023 comes from the Cheryl Hill visit; firelookout.com's staffing note is undated. Access level permission is a judgment from the 2023 post and was not checked against Forest Service rules. Elevation: record 1953.8 m matches the register's 6,410 ft; firelookout.com gives 6,417 ft.
Minor source disagreement on the exact replacement year (1962 vs 1964) and original tower height (100 vs 110 ft); kept both figures in the story/events rather than resolving arbitrarily.

Built timeline (1906/1921/1936/1984) agrees across NHLR, the Forest Service page and firelookout.com; the first-structure year (1905 vs 1906) and elevation (5,595 vs 5,771 ft) conflict. The 1967 Buck Mountain fire entry on the local history site was not used because the page does not clearly tie it to this summit. The July 31, 1984 item is credited to The Register-Guard on the weebly site. Fate of the 1936 L-4 cabin is not documented in the sources checked. The 2018 profile is cited second-hand through the Cheryl Hill page; the staffer is not named in the story. Brief height_m 235.0 is unsupported.

The 1935 Coos Bay Times item and the 1940, 1945 and 1966 newspaper and annual-report entries were read only as quoted on Forest Lookouts, not from the originals. NHLR says the present tower is a 50-foot timber tower but gives no date for it. Status is abandoned per the June 2024 visit and standing per NHLR; both are kept. Administration conflicts: NHLR lists ODF/Coos FPA, the Education Center says DSL manages it for the Common School Fund; not resolved. No official open or closed notice was found, so access is marked restricted as our reading. Brief's height_m 12.2 corrected to 15.2. The Roaming Civic blog is used only for road number and gate pole. No new photos recorded. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the register's administrator line reads Oregon Department of Forestry/Coos FPA; Coos Forest Protective Association is listed only as a cooperator, so the story no longer names it as administrator.

Build year 1955 and the ODF ownership history agree across sources; the building description (14x14 combination lookout vs 3-story enclosed cab) and the access status (NHLR rental listing vs no public access) conflict. The story says the sale date is unknown. Staffing names come from firelookout.com only. The 2022 owner details come from a visit report, not an owner statement. Brief elevation_m 1337.2 is the NHLR figure and is outvoted by three sources. No rental listing was verified.

The 1961 replacement, the 67-foot timber tower and the 2022 register date agree across sources; the brief's 15.2 m height is the earlier 50-foot steel tower, so a correction is proposed. Staffing comes from undated firelookout.com and trail-guide text, so the as_of date is the research date; a current staffing check would strengthen it. Access is restricted to the road and staffed-lookout permission; the sources do not say whether the tower itself is open to visitors, so climbable is omitted. Confidence is high on the build history and medium on current staffing.

Brief record matches the NHLR's 1952 cab date, but firelookout.com calls the 1933 cab the present one. The NHLR and firelookout.com pages are both undated, and the 2014 NHLR visit report is the newest staffing data. Current access is the main open question: the Cool Creek trail page (undated copy) says closed for storm damage, and the Austin and Narrows fire closure (Sept 16 to Dec 31, 2026) boundary text does not name the trail or Still Creek Road; whether it covers this peak was not confirmed. Search snippets said the trail page was updated Jan 5, 2026, and that the Cool Creek trailhead sits in the Zigzag district; neither was read on the page, so neither is used. Search results also included a 1952 date from a photo aggregator, which was not used. No photos added.

Brief's height_m 3.7 has no source in the pages read and is proposed for removal. The 1968 present-cab date is consistent across NHLR, Rex's page and Trails Offroad. Elevation conflict left open: NHLR 7,511 ft vs 7,592 ft on Rex's page and Cheryl Hill. Staffing is from Rex's page (undated, every summer) and a July 2024 visit; current season not confirmed. Name spellings differ across accounts for the 1916 observer (Noey vs Noah Blaine), so no name is used. Forest Lookouts' newspaper items were read as quoted on that site, not from the originals. Trails Offroad is a paid trail-guide site; only its free text was used. Dixie Butte is not on the Malheur NF rental list, which names Fall Mountain Lookout. No new photos recorded. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the L-4 house replaced a cupola cabin of the early 1920s (NHLR), not several early cabins; the 1916 observer phoned the fire's point location, which the story now says.

Brief's design L-4 describes the 1947 cabin, not the cab standing now (two-story, 1997); corrected. Staffing is contested: Rex's page says staffed every summer (undated), while the June 2022 visit found it locked for the season and no one present. Cab size (15 by 15 vs 15 feet 4 inches) and elevation (6,890 vs 6,936 feet) conflict across sources and are both reported. The 1947 structure type conflicts too (L-4 vs Aladdin-style 14 by 14). The 1995 proposal and 1997 build details come from Forest Lookouts quoting Forest Service archive text; not read in the original. Lookout history of Bertha Covert (1918) is from the register; the 1919 and 1920 newspaper item was not used. No photos added; the register and Rex's page carry photo credits that were not checked for license. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 1956 and 1960 Malin items are cited to Forest Lookouts' Herald and News quotes; 'locked up' is now the 2022 visitor's own report that it seemed locked; 6,890 and 6,936 feet are elevations, not summit claims.

Brief's conflict note ('they share a register number') appears to be a brief-generation artifact, not addressed here since no evidence was found that Drake Peak and Bald Butte actually share an NHLR number; NHLR page for Drake Peak gives its own distinct register entry. Flagging for editor to check the queue tool's register-number field if this matters.

Six page reads and one search. The Register, firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill and The Roaming Civic agree on the 1932 build date and the 70-foot height. Forest Lookouts quotes 1929-1934 newspaper items, which are the only source for the 1929 tree platform and the 1931 delivery. Elevation differs: the Register gives 6,241 ft (1,902 m), firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill give 6,281 ft, and the brief's 1902.3 m is the Register figure; not in facts. The Forest Lookouts history gives no fire names. The Facebook post from the Forest Fire Lookout Association could not be read (login wall), so nothing is cited from it. Access level is restricted because the sources describe emergency use and a decommission listing without an open-to-public statement. Current status: the Cheryl Hill directory (July 2026) lists it as unmanned and warns its information may be out of date; the Roaming Civic trip report is undated but post-2017. No photos added. The firelookout.com page credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Rex Kamstra, but no image URLs were extracted.

Height is disputed: the register says a 60-ft CT-2 tower, firelookout.com says 50 ft. No height_m is set and the record has none. The 1941 date agrees across both lookout pages. Staffing comes from a 2023 local news report and a May 2022 register visit, so current status is unconfirmed. History searches turned up nothing beyond these pages. No photos gathered. Visit details are from a single visitor report.

Built date and CCC garage, 1942 AWS conversion and 1999 repair come from the NRHP nomination, the strongest source. Current staffing is unverified: firelookout.com is undated and says staffed in summer; IJPR (2017) uses present tense. No 2025-26 schedule found. Summit elevation differs across sources (7,364, 7,417, 7,418 ft); the record's 2244.5 m matches the register's 7,364 ft. The record's access 'unknown' can be set to public per the sources, but whether the cabin interior is open to visitors is not confirmed. A trail-guide claim that the lookout is still used for emergency fire detection was seen only in a search snippet and not used.

Five page reads and two searches. The build date is the main open question: NHLR and firelookout.com say about 1935, while the agency letters transcribed by Forest Lookouts describe a 1939-1940 purchase and erection, which suggests the 1935 date may be wrong. Reported as a conflict, not resolved. Height 107 ft (32.6 m) agrees across NHLR and firelookout.com. Elevation: NHLR gives 3,168 ft (966 m), firelookout.com and the directory 3,175 ft; the brief's 965.6 m is the NHLR figure and is not in facts. Current status is taken from the Cheryl Hill directory (listed as of July 2026, which warns it may be out of date) and firelookout.com (undated staffing claim). The Madras Pioneer retrospective quotes a line saying the forest service still provided lookouts for three towers in the McQuinn Strip, which does not clearly apply to Eagle Butte, so it is not cited. A 1992 Spilyay Tymoo OCR page mentions a lookout at Eagle Butte, but the OCR is too garbled to quote. No photos added. The 2026 Bench Fire news on the reservation does not mention Eagle Butte in the pages read, so no damage claim is made.

Original 1932 tower and 1995-96 replacement are well documented across sources; the NHLR says 1995 and the Weebly history says 1996 for the finished tower. Elevation (6,371 vs 6,400 ft) and county (Deschutes vs Lake) conflict and are not resolved. The brief height_m 9.1 is the original 30-ft tower, corrected to 6.1 for the current 20-ft tower. The 1959 fire item is from a Bend Bulletin article quoted by the Weebly site. The 2023 'not invited up' remark is one visitor's account and is not an official access rule. The Roaming Civic 2023 title and date come from a search result; the quoted lines were fetched from its page. firelookout.com says the 1995 structure is a replica of the original 30-foot tower, while the NHLR and Cheryl Hill say 20 feet. The record uses 20 feet (6.1 m) and the story attributes the 20-foot figure to the NHLR. This conflict is not in the story.

County conflict: the register says Union County, firelookout.com says Wallowa County; the story keeps the firelookout.com wording and says the register places it in Union County. The 1966 object was identified as a balloon in the same clipping, and the story now says so. Early history unsettled: the 1928 patrolman item and firelookout.com's 1928 staff entry predate the 1933 build year, and the 1932 plan for a 25 ft tower with a 14x14 house may or may not be the 1933 tower. Record height is not used because the sources give 10 to 40 ft. Ownership conflict: the register lists USFS as administrator while firelookout.com and the directory describe private land; the agency field keeps the register wording with a note. Elevation: 5,127 ft (register) vs 5,122 ft (firelookout); the record's 1562.7 m matches the register. Register photo credit (Ray Kresek, 1993) noted but no image URL was found, so no photo added. Record status 'standing' kept; the cab is abandoned.

Sources conflict on the cupola date (1921 register and 1921 newspaper vs 1924 in two others), the 1936 tower height (20, 29 or 30 ft), and whether the tower is in the rental program (2015 removal per a 2026 blog vs rental until pulled for 2022 per a 2022 trip report vs an FS page offering overnight rental). Current access is unresolved: FS marks the site open with a rental, Travel Oregon says temporarily closed, and a 2026 visitor found the road gated. Staffing after 2024 is hearsay from a TikTok account, which also describes a few days of staffing in July 2025. Elevation differs across sources (NHLR 5,857 ft; Roaming Civic 5,933 ft; firelookout 5,933 ft); the brief's 1785.2 m matches NHLR. No source found on any fire spotted from the tower. The brief's built 1972 refers to the present tower; the first structure dates to 1912.

The tower record's build-year conflict (1930 vs 1933) resolves fairly well once the NHLR page is read in full: it describes an emergency post dating to around 1930/1933 with the cab original but the tower rebuilt in 1953 — a detail not yet in the tower JSON's events. No newspaper or Forest Service administrative-history source was found in the cache or a quick web check; everything here comes from the three register/rental pages already linked on the record. Did not propose a correction since the conflict is explainable rather than contradictory, but an editor may want to add the 1953 tower-rebuild event to the main tower record.
No current staffing status found in sources, so staffing left as unknown rather than guessed; the brief's 1957 built-year is confirmed by all three sources.

Present-cab year conflicts: register and Wikipedia say 1960, firelookout.com says 1966. Record height_m 2.4 is wrong; proposed 16.2 m from firelookout.com's 53 ft, which may be overall height. firelookout.com also describes a 30-foot Snowshoe lookout a mile east; the story omits it because the sources give little detail. The 2025 staffing is from the register; the 2023 notice is from a local news report. No drive-up or trail information found. No photos gathered.

Height of the 1953 tower is disputed: register says 40 ft laminated wood, firelookout.com says 50 ft wooden. The record's height_m 15.2 matches firelookout.com only; left as is, not changed. Access (private, no public access) and staffing (into the 2010s) come only from firelookout.com; the register says in active service without a date. Few sources were available, and the searches found no ODF or Wikipedia history. No photos gathered. Treat the access claim as needing confirmation before publishing.

Disputed 1926 damage: the register says the cupola burned, Bend newspapers of August 1926 say the lookout tower was destroyed, and a January 1927 report says the tower was not burned but two supports were. The story says the sources disagree. Elevation: the register gives 6,065 ft (the record's 1848.6 m); firelookout.com and the 2021 directory give 6,025 ft. Record matches the register; not changed. Current status: the 2021 visitor wrote that the Forest Service proposed removal; the FS project page (last updated Feb 2025) lists it cancelled, so the removal threat may be over but no current agency statement was found. Access: gated road, not a public visit; the story recommends not climbing. Newspaper transcriptions are on the weebly page and were not checked against original newspaper scans.

Six page reads and one search. The brief's height_m of 2.1 is a clear error (100 ft, about 30.5 m) and is proposed as a correction. The brief's 1940 build date comes from the NHLR's ground house sentence and is contradicted by the tower dates of 1936-37 elsewhere. The Roaming Civic history also says a 4-year-old boy fell from a landing and died, attributed to the Fire Lookouts of the Northwest book; it gives no date and no second source, so it is left out of the story. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a Glendale Log item from January 1937 and a Burns Times-Herald item from 1943. Story says the 1930s first site was a point about half a mile away; the sources differ on direction (firelookout says southeast, Cheryl Hill says south). Status: NHLR (2019 survey) and Cheryl Hill (2021) describe the tower as condemned and slated for removal; the July 2026 directory calls the site abandoned but legally accessible and warns its information may be out of date. The tower's current condition after 2022 is unverified. The FFLA Facebook post in the search results was not fetched. No photos added; firelookout.com credits photos to the U.S. Forest Service, National Archives and Records Administration, and Rex Kamstra, but no image URLs were extracted.

The renaming year (1946 on two sites), the end of staffing (1973 in the register, 1960s on firelookout.com) and restoration status all conflict and are reported as such. The brief's L-4 design is kept; the register adds that the cab is an updated BC-301 version. A search snippet from cherylhill.net gives 1944 for the renaming; that page was not read in full, so it is not used. Restoration status is the most likely to be stale and should be rechecked before publishing. Access is marked public for the trail only; the sources do not say whether the cabin can be entered, and the Forest Service warns about its condition, so the story does not encourage entry.

Unresolved: 1934 tower height (66 ft in a 1934 newspaper vs 50 ft on firelookout.com). Rebuild year 1968 (NHLR, 1968 report) vs 1969 (firelookout.com, 1969 report); the 1968 and 1969 reports both describe the same winter, so the year depends on how the reports count. Staffing 'every summer' comes from an undated page; the latest dated staffing in the pages read is 1965. No rental information found. Record access 'unknown' can be set to private (NHLR and firelookout.com agree).

Elevation conflict: brief/NHLR give 4,477 ft (1,365 m), Recreation.gov gives 4,618 ft. Left out of story text since it's a minor figure; see corrections entry. Fact-check 2026-10-04: all three citations re-fetched and verified verbatim against the live sources, including the Recreation.gov Directions section ('last 2 miles of road access are rough gravel and dirt at a 10 percent uphill grade'), which backs the story's 'rough gravel roads' detail though it falls outside the short evidence quote on file. No unsupported claims or citation errors found; no edits needed to the story text.

Brief's 2011 build year is supported by NHLR and the Oregon Lookouts history page; firelookout.com and Roaming Civic say 2010 (contract and work year). Unresolved: a 1964 newspaper says the first house was built 'last summer', but BLM bids were not called until October 1963, so the 1963 build season is uncertain; the story says 1963 with the caveat. Brief's record lacks the 1963 predecessor and its 10-foot base; events added. height_m 15.2 is the 50-foot tower. Elevation sources: NHLR 5,188 ft, firelookout.com 5,190 ft; brief 1581.3 m kept. Staffing is undated (firelookout.com). Access is 'restricted' from a 2022 gated campground, not from any BLM access rule; no rental found. Sources 3 and 4 show the 1963 tower's wooden live-in cab; minor distance conflict (19 vs 20 miles) not used in story.

Sources disagree on the first structure (1912 alidade, 1916 cabin, 1920 cupola, 1923 original per Gazette-Times) and on how the L-4 cab reached the site. No end date for staffing was found; the Register's 'no longer man' note is undated. Visitor access is not documented. Elevation conflicts: 3,835 ft (NHLR) vs 3,977 ft (firelookout, cherylhill). No photos added. Search surfaced an ODF Facebook post and an Oregon SOS record photo caption, not read.
A 2014 Country Roads magazine PDF is linked from the NHLR page (not fetched here, within budget) and could add staffing-era detail if a future pass wants more depth.

Unresolved: distance from Gold Beach (about five miles in 1937, about four miles east in 1942, two miles southeast on firelookout.com). Storm date: December 1941 per a Dec 17, 1941 paper and a Feb 1942 article, 1942 per NHLR, 'last January' per a March 1942 article. Current status: the cab was converted to a radio building per firelookout.com (undated); no source read says whether it is open, staffed or rentable, so access is left out. Staffing after 1941 is thin: a February 1942 account names Emmett Freeman as stationed there during air-raid warning use; no other staffing after 1941 was found in the pages read, apart from a 1966 Forest Service lookout report whose site name is garbled in the source. Record kind 'ground' and elevation 710.8 m fit the current structure.

The tower record's 'conflicts' block (built: 1967 per NHLR vs 1912 per firelookout_com) is resolved by reading the prose on both cached pages rather than just their structured fields: both agree on a sequence (1912 octagonal cab -> 1936 L-4 -> 1967 R-6, the structure standing today), they just populate a single 'built' field with different points in that sequence. Recommend the record's events array capture the full sequence rather than one disputed year. NHLR's '1915' for first fire detection is one source only (not independently corroborated) and sits oddly close to, but not matching, the 1912 build year on firelookout.com -- plausibly detection started a few years before any structure went up, but this is not stated outright anywhere, so I left it as a direct citation rather than resolving it further. No additional cached source pages or useful web leads were found beyond NHLR, firelookout.com, and the Recreation.gov listing already in the tower record; did not use any of the 3 allotted web searches since the two cached register pages already agreed with each other almost completely once read past their structured fields. Fact-check correction: the draft's claim that NHLR's prose 'notes the discrepancy itself' between a 1915 fire-detection date and 'the register's own account of the first cab' was wrong -- NHLR's description never mentions a first cab or any 1912/1936 structure at all (only '...fire detection site since 1915. The current structure was constructed in 1967... roof was modified... in 1992.'); the 1912/1936 sequence comes solely from firelookout.com. That sentence was removed from the story. Also fixed: the story's 'flat-topped summit' was an invented/confused descriptor (likely conflated with the R-6 'flat top' cabin design) with no support in either cached source, so it was dropped; the elevation figure (7,188 ft) was misattributed to the Recreation.gov footnote when it is actually NHLR's number -- Recreation.gov's own page gives 7,195 ft, confirmed live. Both numbers are now attributed to their correct sources. All other checked claims (1912/1936/1967/1992 sequence, 2022 NHLR registration and Brad Eells nomination, rental season Nov 15-May 15, cabin dimensions/beds/stoves/capacity/no water, foot-snowshoe-ski-only access, Mount Hood/Shasta views) were confirmed against the cited sources and a live fetch of the Recreation.gov page.

Thin record: no staff lists, fires or construction records were found beyond the 1938 build date. The Living New Deal page on CCC construction at the Pine Ranger Station returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Height: record's 2.1 m is wrong; 52 ft is consistent across the register and firelookout.com. Elevation: register 2,566 ft vs 2,600 ft on firelookout.com and the 2013 visit; the 2,600 figure is probably rounded to the nearest hundred feet, but no source says so. Access and status are an informal emergency-use situation at an active Forest Service office; the story keeps climbing discouraged. The Roaming Civic and cherylhill pages are visitor accounts, not agency records.

Build year conflict: 1956 (register, firelookout.com, cherylhill.net) vs a 1957 completion in newspaper items quoted on the Oregon Lookouts page. Elevation: the register gives 4,470 ft (1,362 m), matching the record's 1362.5 m; cherylhill.net gives 5,006 ft, not used. Access 'public' is inferred from a 2023 visit account, not a Forest Service rule; check before publishing. Whetstone burned (register) vs removed (cherylhill.net) in 1958 concerns a different site. No fire history found; no WebSearch used. Visitor names in source pages are left out on purpose.

Dates: 1925 newspaper item (house being built for a lookout) vs 1934 first L-4 cabin per three sites; the 1954 cab is consistent across all four sources. Elevation: NHLR 5,983 ft (1,824 m) matches the record's 1823.6 m; cherylhill.net gives 6,071 ft, not used. Access 'public' is inferred from the staffed status and a 2023 visit; gate status and road end are unverified. Staffer's and families' names in the newspaper items are left out. josephoregon.us appeared in search results but was not read or cited. Oregon Lookouts newspaper quotes come via that page, not the original papers.

Current access is the main open question: the Forest Service closure of Aug 2024 is about two years old, the closure length was undetermined, and no reopening notice was found. Verify with the Wallowa Mountains front desk 541-426-5546. The Battle Creek Fire caption has no year and the name is unconfirmed; a Hells Canyon Scenic Byway post (1989 fire) returned HTTP 404 twice and was not used. Elevation differs: register 6,960 ft (record 2121.4 m matches), firelookout.com 6,982 ft. Oregon Hikers says 80 ft and climbing allowed; its page footer says last modified 27 July 2025, after the Aug 2024 closure. That is an edit date, so the guide's climbing text may still predate the closure. A WTA search snippet (not read) says climbing access ended years ago. Staffing as_of 2005 rests on one visit report and an undated firelookout.com line; the 2024 closure also stopped administrative use of the cab, so current staffing is doubtful.

Record height_m 12.2 is not supported by any page read here, so it is not in facts; check its source. Elevation 1040.0 m matches NHLR (3,412 ft / 1,040 m). Location conflict: NHLR says 'north of Bend'; firelookout.com and a 1953 item say 5-6 miles from Sisters; the 2014 Bulletin says roughly a mile. The first tower's height (40 vs 42 ft) and date (1940s vs 1943) conflict. A 2020 Central Oregonian search snippet says the first lookout was built in the 1930s; it was not read and is not cited. The 1953 and 1958 lookouts and the 2014 staffer are named in the sources; their names are left out. Access 'restricted' comes from one 2021 blog visit; no ODF statement was read. Name origin rests on the Roaming Civic alone.

Good multi-source agreement on build date, design, and NRHP listing. The 'refurbished in the 1980s' date is vague (onX source only gives decade); no need to correct the brief's current record, which already matches these facts closely. Fact-check 2026-10-04: the 1913 fire-plan sentence was footnoted to source 1 (NHLR) but the supporting quote is from source 6 (weebly); corrected to [^6]. The story said the design was standard for 'Region 6 (then District 1)' lookouts, which inverts the actual history per the NRHP form (it was District Six, later renamed Region Six); corrected. The vacant/period-of-significance sentence cited source 6 (weebly), which does not support it; dropped, kept source 4 (NRHP) only. The living-quarters/ladder sentence copied the NRHP form's wording too closely; rewritten. The views sentence (Crater Lake, Thielsen, Bailey, McLoughlin, Shasta) had no footnote though it is directly supported by source 5 (Hiking Project); added [^5]. Spot-checked the Osborne firefinder alidade and three-sided catwalk claims directly against the NRHP document text; both confirmed verbatim.

Construction dates for the present tower differ across four sources (1952, 1953, 1954, early 1950s); the story reports the disagreement. The Water Bureau's 2022 article names the contractor; the story leaves the name out. Water Bureau article gives a 2022 renewal request with no outcome found. Mt. Hood NF Facebook post (Oct 17, 2022) says staffed each summer since built; not used. Trail Advocates archive and a 2022 Portland council impact statement were surfaced by search but not read. No photos added. Height_m 12.5 is a unit conversion of the 41-foot figure.

Original and present tower heights, the 1959 vs 1960 replacement date, and the 100 ft USGS survey figure all conflict across sources; reported in the story. The directory's staffing status is as of July 2026. Lookout staff names listed on firelookout.com were left out of the story. No photos added; the Register and firelookout.com credit photos to the Umatilla NF and a private collection, and were not checked for licensing. The NHLR page also has 2003 and 2005 visit reports and a 2016 photo gallery that were not read.

Access is unresolved: the directory and Rex's page disagree, and no ODF page was found. A Herald and News article ('Hiking the Hog') may help but returned HTTP 429 when fetched, so it is not cited. The register's 1941 first-tower date was not confirmed by any other source read. Confirm with ODF Klamath-Lake District before changing access level.

Unresolved: the crow's nest tree is 65 feet in the register and 110 feet in the nomination; the register's 65-foot figure may describe a different tree, so the story reports both. Brief's 1935 build year is proposed for correction (see corrections). The 2001 cabin work is 'cleaned and covered openings' in the nomination but 'restored' in the 2023 visit report; both are reported. Staffing end year (1970) is approximate. The 2015 fire-break explanation is the blogger's guess and is not used as fact. Current condition comes from one June 2023 visit and the 2014-era nomination; no later source checked. Rental never happened per the 2023 visit. Access set to restricted: Forest Service land with a gated road and removed stairs. Tower 100 ft (height_m 30.5); nomination says 101 ft.

Early history is disputed. firelookout.com (one source, undated) gives a 1932 platform tower half a mile southeast of the summit; the register places a sawn-timber lookout on the southern point and its first tower on the northern point in 1934. Built field 1960 versus description 1961 (correction proposed). Staffing is undated: the register says 'in recent years' and firelookout.com says 'in the summer'. No public access level, climbing rule or rental listing was found. Staffing as_of left out for lack of a date. The 1970s standby is in the story but has no event entry, because the register gives no year.

Brief height_m 1.8 is wrong (100-foot tower); see corrections. Build year (1941 vs 1942 finish vs 1946 in a 2019 newspaper) and cab size (7x7 vs 6x6) are unresolved. Firelookout.com is undated, so 'abandoned' is not dated. No source found on current public access, climbing or rental; access and visit keys omitted. Staffing names come from firelookout.com only. No new photo with a reusable licence was found.

The brief's height_m value (1.2) looks like a data error for an L-4 ground house with a catwalk -- no source supports a 1.2 m height, and no source consulted gives a tower/cab height figure at all, so height_m was omitted here rather than carried forward or guessed. The access level in the existing record (public) looks too permissive given this is a staffed, operational lookout; flagged as a correction above.

Tower date: 1955 (register), 1956 (firelookout.com), 1958 (Eugene Weekly). Height: 20 feet (register and firelookout.com) versus 30 feet (Eugene Weekly). Staffing: 'still staffed each year' (register, undated) versus 'available for emergencies' (firelookout.com, undated); not resolved. Rental status not found. The Library of Congress HABS record OR-197 (loc.gov/item/or0638) returned HTTP 403 and was not read, so it is not cited; a search summary of it gave a 1956 tower and a 1920 firefinder, which should be checked. Eugene Weekly mentions a locked trap door on the 1958 tower; the story does not encourage climbing it. Height and tower date were left out of facts for these reasons.
Brief's build year (1957) matches NHLR; firelookout.com/recreation.gov say 1958, so this is a genuine one-year source conflict (noted in the story and resolved_conflicts), not a brief error.

Sources 2 and 3 are the same page cited for two different facts, as allowed. The Crockets Knob Fire's effect on the structure itself is ambiguous in the only source found (a blog category page, not the full post); a reviewer with time to fetch the individual cherylhill.net post could confirm whether the lookout survived undamaged. Current brief's 'access: unknown' should be updated to reflect that it is an active staffed station, not a rental. Fact-check 2026-10-04: every footnoted sentence in the story checked out against its cited evidence, including the specific month details (December 1929, September 1957) and the 'Blue Mountain Eagle' attribution, none of which appeared verbatim in the evidence excerpts but all of which were confirmed by re-fetching the weebly source directly. The July 3, 2022 NHLR registration date was also confirmed directly against the NHLR page. No unsupported claims or copied wording found; no edits needed.

Only two sources were readable and they agree on the 1952 tower and the 1938 L-4 it replaced. Staffing 'every summer' and the personnel years are undated. No rental listing or public access rule was found. Searches surfaced a 2005 geocache listing and a 2008 forum trip report; neither was used as a citation (the geocache page yielded only its title). Personnel names from firelookout.com are left out of the story. Elevation was not recorded in facts: the register gives 5,702 ft and firelookout.com gives 5,714 ft.

Status and access rest on a July 2021 visit report; the removal proposal is undated and no newer report was found, so current status is unverified. Early build dates conflict (1920s cupola and 1933 cabin per register; 1923 cupola per two other sources). The register's Ochocco reference looks like an error for Malheur. The record's height_m 5.5 m is not supported by the sources read. Elevation: the register gives 6,645 ft (2,025 m), matching the record; a peakbagging.com photo page gives 6,683 ft, not read. Not read in full: the 1987 inspection notes and the 1956 bid correspondence (both on the Forest Lookouts page), and a Malheur NF facility plan mentioned on Cheryl Hill's site. Staffing after 2021 is unknown.

Mountain name spelled 'Barkalow' by NHLR and 'Barklow' by Recreation.gov; treated as the same place, not flagged as a conflict. Tower height (10 ft vs 12 ft) differs between the two sources and is called out in the story and resolved_conflicts. Did not independently verify the exact trailhead/drive-up access; Recreation.gov implies a hike in with no on-site water.

Core dates (1931 first lookout, 1998 current structure, 2003 register) agree across all three pages. Open: staffing and whether the cab is open to visitors are not established by any page read. Elevation differs slightly (NHLR 4,958 ft; Firelookout.com 5016 ft; Wikipedia summit 5,020 ft) and was left out of the story. A search snippet suggested a 1913 telephone line and an earlier cabin; the full page was not read, so it is not used. The brief's record of a 1998 build is correct for the present tower but omits the 1931 original.

Current access and staffing rest on the Forest Service page (undated in our copy; treated as 2026). The 2004 restoration rests only on Oregon Hikers, a volunteer-edited wiki; the 2004 scanned report cited in the brief (firelookout.org cr-or-2004.pdf) has no text layer and could not be machine-checked, so it is not used. The brief's 2004 rental-program claim comes from that same PDF and is omitted; no source read mentions a rental program. Firelookout.com also gives elevation 4255 ft; search snippets (not read as pages) also show 4,236 ft (Oregon Hikers) and 4243 ft (Outerspatial). The story reports only the register and Forest Service figures. The Bedrock Fire is named with no date (none found in sources read), so the story gives no year. The brief record's elevation_m 1215.5 matches the register. The brief record had only the 1960 build; the 1923 cupola and 1967 standby events are added from the register.

Brief's kind 'two_story' is not supported by the sources read: the register calls it a flattop 14x14 lookout and Cheryl Hill calls it a ground cabin; firelookout.org's list says '2-Story cab' but was not cited. Brief's height_m 4.3 has no supporting source in the pages read, so it is not in facts. Elevation in the brief matches the register. Forest Lookouts' 'Waldo Mountain' versus 'Waldo Hill' is unresolved beyond the register and Rex's agreeing on Waldo Hill. Two ODF or Forest Service pages were not checked.

Height correction is the main fix to the brief (18.3 m is the 1935 tower). Heights for the present tower differ across sources (82, 87, 90 ft). Location and elevation differ between the brief and the register; not changed. The 1947 newspaper plan gave 83 ft and was not confirmed as built at that height. Walla Walla ranger district office or Umatilla NF recreation page not read; they may confirm current staffing and access.

Current condition rests on one July 2024 visitor blog. No 2025-26 source was read. Forest Service pages were not fetched; a Fremont-Winema trailhead page appeared in search and was not read. The 1931, 1932 and 1947 newspaper items are only as transcribed on oregonlookouts.weebly.com; originals not checked. Unresolved: the 1932 Bend Bulletin item says the legs were sixteen feet high, while later sources say the tower was 20 ft; the story says the sources differ. Photos not added: no image URL with a confirmed license.

The 1950s abandonment is given only as a decade, so the year 1950 in events is a placeholder. The 1925 fireman posting is a plan from a July 1925 report, not confirmed by NHLR or firelookout.com, so no staffed_first event is recorded. The Forest Lookouts page shows a 'Removed' label next to the site after its photo credits; its meaning is unclear and it conflicts with NHLR and firelookout.com, which both describe standing structures, so 'standing' is kept with a note. The record's height_m 1.8 is not supported by any page read. NHLR photo credits (1940 and 1955 Forest Service) are not added as new finds.

Brief's NHLR registration date (July 4, 2022) was not in the NHLR text I read, so no nhlr_registered event is recorded; the NHLR page was read only for location, elevation, build and design. Registry numbers US 1632 / OR 150 and the Standing status appear on the Forest Fire Lookout Association standing list (read during the McGraw task; not cited as evidence here). Firelookout.com's staffing line is undated; as_of 2024 comes from the May 2024 visit page. Search snippets mentioned a 2024 trailhead closure and a 2023 staffed trip report; neither was read, so neither is in the story. A 1981 helicopter accident at the lookout site (quoted on the Forest Lookouts page) is omitted for length. Access is marked restricted because the cab's status for visitors is not stated in any source read; no climb is encouraged. Reads: 5 pages plus one re-read of the Forest Lookouts page; 2 web searches.

Brief's registration date (July 4, 2022) and registry numbers US 1633 / OR 151 are confirmed on the NHLR page. Brief's height_m of 3.0 is wrong; corrected to 25.0. No access level is recorded: no source read says whether the public can visit or climb the tower, so the access key is omitted. A search snippet mentioned a Hells Canyon MVUM legend with a Cabin Rental entry near Imnaha; it was not tied to McGraw and was not read, so it is not used. The 1930s staffing name differs between sources (Cleve Loyd vs I.C. Loyd). Firelookout.com's abandoned statement is undated. Reads: 4 pages (NHLR, firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts, FFLA standing list); 2 web searches.

Elevation conflict, not resolved: the register gives 7,180 ft (2,188 m), which matches the record's elevation_m; firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill give 7,234 ft (about 2,205 m). Origin site is disputed: the Round Pass record (US 1040) gives 7,462 ft at the pass, while Cheryl Hill places the earlier cabin on Round Mountain, also 7,462 ft. The 2020 Brattain Fire is mentioned only by the 2024 staffer; the fire itself was not checked, and a search turned up Paisley news reports that were not read. Staffing and access rest on a July 2024 visit and an undated firelookout.com page; nothing newer was found. Weebly page read only in targeted lines.

Brief had no height; height_m 12.2 is 40 feet converted to metres. Access level omitted: no source states whether the site is public or closed; the 2012 account describes a rough road and a hike of about 1.8 miles. Second-tower date (late 1930s vs 1942) and 1957 construction material are unresolved. No staffing record after 1954 found. A 2012 account is the newest status evidence.

Brief's record checks: registration July 5, 2022 and US 1338 / OR 153 are confirmed on the NHLR page; the 1916 build date is confirmed. The brief's 'ground' kind matches NHLR, but a 2023 visit page calls it a steel tower. No access level is firmly established: the sources say the lookout is staffed and reachable on a 3.5-mile trail, but not whether the cab is open to visitors, so access is marked restricted. The 2021 article's staffing outcome is not confirmed beyond the June 9 statement. Search snippets mention a Whitman Ranger District phone number, a Wikipedia elevation of 8,325 ft and a 2021 Blue Mountain Eagle version; none were read, so none are used. Reads: 6 pages (NHLR, firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts, 2023 visit page, 2021 La Grande Observer article); 2 web searches.

The 1964 build year and the 1923/1929/1933 sequence agree across sources. Staffing is from undated firelookout.com text and an undated register line; the only access report is a 2011 blog visit, so current road and cab-access status is unverified. Design wording differs slightly (NHLR says wooden; firelookout.com says treated timber), and both were kept as timber. Elevation is 6,800 ft per NHLR and 6816 ft per firelookout.com. The 2008 burn was a patrol point, not the lookout. Not read: the Ochoco National Forest pages and the Facebook FFLA post.

Current status is consistent across the register (emergency use), firelookout.com (available for emergencies) and the 2024 blog (not staffed, USGS equipment). The founding date is disputed (1923, 1924, or 1924/25 with the house built 1929). Elevation differs: NHLR 8,806 ft; firelookout.com 8926 ft; Wikipedia 8,934 ft (not used in the story). The NHLR 1977 visit report lists staffing as Sometimes; not used because it is dated. The brief's agency 'U.S. Dept. of the Interior' matches the register; the NPS is named as cooperator. Willhite Web is a personal history site that reproduces park files; treat its dates as secondary. Not read: any Crater Lake NPS page on visitor access to the cab.

The record's 'built 1947' is the replacement date; the first tower is 1932 per NHLR text, firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts. Access is not stated by any source read, so no access level is given. Elevation differs across sources (NHLR 4,665 ft, firelookout.com 4715 ft, Wikidata 4,695 ft) and the record's 1421.9 m was left alone. Staffing as_of is the NHLR 'mid 1980s' wording because the pages are undated. Cherylhill.net also gives 1946 for the replacement but was not fetched.

Built year is approximate (NHLR says as early as 1924; firelookout.com has a question mark). The 1916 heliograph placement conflicts: NHLR ties it to Mule Peak, the 1916 newspaper item quoted by Oregon Lookouts places it on Granite Butte; both kept, unresolved. Staffing and today's status rest on one 2025 blog trip report and a 1980s name from firelookout.com; no Forest Service document found. Access 'restricted' is an inference from the locked cab and staffing; no official visitor policy found. Judy Wing is named only as a historical lookout attendant. One websearch used. Cheryl Hill's standing-lookouts list marks Mule Peak unmanned, which conflicts with the 2025 trip report; both are reported. Record access 'unknown' and staffing 'unknown' could be updated from the sources above.

Staffing and the current tower date rest on visitor blogs and an undated firelookout.com page. The 1915, 1927, 1942 and 1962 newspaper items are only as transcribed on oregonlookouts.weebly.com; originals not checked. No Forest Service or Deschutes National Forest page was read. Photos not added: firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Gary Weber, but no image URLs or licenses were confirmed.

Current rental is closed to reservations (confirmed live on Recreation.gov as of 2026-10-04), consistent with Firelookout.com's note that the site is presently abandoned; treated access as 'restricted' rather than fully 'public' to flag that. Minor year discrepancy on the first platform tower (1915 vs 1916).

Build year (1933), tower height (72 ft) and CCC origin agree across the register, firelookout.com and the 2024 blog. Purpose is unresolved: firelookout.com says it was primarily for wildlife observation; Cheryl Hill doubts it was used for fire detection. Current status and access rest on an April 2024 blog visit and the register's undated text; nothing newer was found. The 2024 blog's tower-height conflict (80/90/99 ft) concerns a different refuge tower (the headquarters tower, US 429), not this one. Wikipedia's P Ranch article (NRHP 1979) describes the ranch and was read but not used for the lookout. The fws.gov Malheur cultural heritage page appeared in search and was not read.

The 3.0 m height in the record is wrong (see corrections). Heights (40 vs 50 ft), cab size and cause and year of loss (arson 1995 vs vandals or arson 1996) conflict across sources, so the story reports the disagreement. A 1937 newspaper line describes the old tower as 50 feet above the rocky top, which does not square with the 30 ft 1934 tower named by the Register and firelookout.com; not reconciled. Current staffing rests on undated firelookout.com plus the June 2022 visit. Access is recorded as permission because the gate sign on Green Diamond land grants revocable recreational use; no public-entry rule for the tower was found.

The 1991-2012 repair chronology rests mainly on the Sand Mountain Society page, written by the group that did the work; the register corroborates the 1954 replacement and the 1994 completion, and firelookout.com corroborates the 1920 start. The record's access 'public' is not stated outright in the sources read: the society opens the lookout each spring and says visitors have made changes, but it posts no visitor rules. Confirm before treating public visiting as established. Staffing is set to unknown; no source read describes fire staffing. The record's 2008 'modified' and 2011/2012 restorations come from the society page, so they are supported by one source. Firelookout.com places the lookout '13 miles northwest of Cave Junction' and the society places it '10 miles WNW of Selma'; the story uses the society's location. The society names the agency 'Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest'; the register says 'Siskiyou National Forest' and the story does not name the forest.

Minor unresolved discrepancy on exactly which restoration campaign (1991 SMS/Jim Borders re-roofing, a Pete Bond-led Oregon State Parks restoration per NHLR, or a 1995 date per firelookout.com) is the 'main' one; these may all be real, sequential volunteer efforts. Current brief listed access as 'public' which matches what we found; staffing/status fields can be added since the brief omitted them. Fact-check 2026-10-04: the story described John Oblack as a 'Czech stonemason's helper,' which isn't in any source (source 1/BLM calls him 'a Czechoslovakian from Molalla with help from an unknown stone mason from Portland,' i.e. Oblack built it himself with an unnamed mason's help, not the other way around); corrected to match the source wording. Spot-checked the 1918 rangefinder-only origin and the 'four sides / 360-degree view' claim directly against the BLM page, and the 1991 'autumn rains' re-roofing detail directly against the Sand Mountain Society page; all three confirmed. The 'only stone lookout remaining in Oregon' claim was also confirmed on the BLM page (not previously quoted in the evidence list, but present in the source).

Current status (standby, used only in emergencies, unmanned) rests on NHLR, firelookout.com and an undated standing-lookouts list; no Forest Service document was found and the present road and visitor status is unverified. The first-structure date conflicts: 1934 newspapers (tower erected, station under construction) versus firelookout.com's 1935. The 1980 newspaper item and the 1986 date for the present cab do not line up cleanly; the 1980 item describes a 39-foot tower and a lookout to be stationed the next summer. Elevation: register 7,994 ft (2,437 m) matches the record; firelookout.com and the standing-lookouts list give 8,035 ft. Staffing 'unstaffed' as_of 'undated' is from the standing-lookouts list and standby status. Access 'restricted' is an inference, not an official policy. One websearch (unproductive) and five page reads were used for this tower.

Build-year conflict between NHLR (1958) and recreation.gov/firelookout.com (1934 original, 1948 current tower) is unresolved; flagged in both the story and resolved_conflicts. height_m corrected to ~12.5 (41-ft tower) in facts; the original brief's 7.6 figure appears to have been cab-only or an error and has been applied/fixed. Fact-check 2026-10-04 also found and fixed a footnote misattribution (the homesteader sentence cited firelookout.com, which never mentions 1898/Pickett, instead of recreation.gov) and a cab-dimension conflict between NHLR (14'x14') and recreation.gov (12x12) that the brief had not flagged; both are now noted in the story and resolved_conflicts.

Coordinates disagree: the Register gives N 43.264680, W 122.264680, while the record's longitude of -122.37989 (and 43.2642 latitude) differs by about 0.11 degrees, roughly 9 km. Not resolved in the record; the editor should check the coordinates against the Register and a map before any change. Current status rests on a 2023 visitor report and the undated Roaming Civic post; no 2025-26 source read. Forest Service trail page and an FFLA Facebook post were seen in search but not read. The 1950 and 1951 staffing items and the 1962 News-Review item are only as transcribed on oregonlookouts.weebly.com; originals not checked. Photos not added: no image URLs or licenses confirmed.

Staffing (seasonal, as_of 2012) rests on firelookout.com's undated 'staffed every summer', a 2012 visit report and an undated standing-lookouts list; no Forest Service source found. Access 'restricted' is inferred from the staffed cab and a 2012 visitor not being invited up; the road's current condition is unverified. Two record corrections: height_m 9.1 is the 1931 pole tower, and design 'L-4' omits the 82-ft tower. Omitted on purpose: a 1961 fatal fall from this tower, reported in a Bend Bulletin item quoted by Oregon Lookouts; it is not part of the lookout's fire-watch history, so the editor may want to decide whether to add it. Elevation: register 6,710 ft and the record's 2045.2 m agree; firelookout.com and the standing-lookouts list give 6,745 ft.

Not a tower: the record's point kind is right, and the NHLR page describes an Osborne fire-finder in an enclosure. Build date is approximate (circa 1930s). The 1935 panorama note does not say who Osborne was, so the story does not link him to the finder's name. No fires, named staff or closure history were found in the sources read. Access: the finder is locked and used only in emergencies, and the pull-out is on a public road, so access is rated restricted. Photos on the NHLR and firelookout.com pages are credited to Rex Kamstra, but no image URLs were captured, so none are added. One search returned a Forest Fire Lookout Association history page of the Osborne finder (firelookout.org/resources/plans/hist-osborne/) that was not read; it could add build and staffing detail. Cheryl Hill's table header was read on 2026-10-08: Unmanned is the STATUS column, and the last column is Accessible to Public (legal access only, per the directory's own note).

Current rental status needs a check closer to publication — recreation.gov shows it closed to reservations 'until further notice' and firelookout.com attributes this to storm damage, but neither gives a date for the storm or an expected reopening. Brief's rental.available=true is likely stale. Fact-check 2026-10-04 found the story had wrongly dated NHLR registration to 'the mid-1990s' (actually March 2003, per NHLR) and had overstated current staffing: NHLR's own 2007/2015 volunteer visit reports say the tower was unstaffed and, by 2015, badly deteriorated. Both fixed in the story and logged above.

Record's design 'L-4' conflicts with NHLR's ODF 14 x 14 cab and with the 1946 district report. Build date conflicts (1930s first cab; 1946 district report; NHLR 1950). Land status conflicts: NHLR says BLM land, firelookout.com says private property with no public access; access level set to private pending confirmation. No source read is dated after 2003 except the Forest Lookouts history, which ends in the 1960s, so current condition is unverified. Forest Lookouts quotes a 1946 district report and 1963 to 1966 district reports. Spelling varies, Rancheria and Rancherie. Photos not added.

Height correction is the main finding: the record's 6.1 m matches the earlier 20 ft pole tower, not the present 41 ft tower. The 1943 new-tower item conflicts with the 1953 build date and is unexplained in sources read. Rental and access status are unconfirmed. A Forest Service Umpqua camping and cabins page (fs.usda.gov/r06/umpqua/recreation/camping-cabins) appeared in search but was not read. A Library of Congress record for the tower (loc.gov/item/or0645/) returned HTTP 403, so it is not used. Its search snippet describes an L-4 Standard '36 cab on a 41 ft TT-1 tower; check it before relying on that model. Cheryl Hill's Lookout Mountain blog (June 2024) may bear on the planned move but was not read. Photos: NHLR credits a 2015 photo to Dennis Poulin and firelookout.com credits one to Dominic Luebbers; no image URLs were captured, so none are added.

Build dates conflict (1936, 1947 vs 1949 for the current tower). Status conflicts: firelookout.com says abandoned; the 2022 visit and the list say standing. The brief's height_m 3.0 looks wrong (correction proposed). Staffing as_of is the 2022 visit, not a staffing report. Stair removal is from a single 2022 visitor account; no current FS status page was found, so the climbing status should be checked before anyone visits.

The record's name and coordinates describe the relocated cabin at Tiller, which is right. Its elevation (1462 m, 4,797 ft) matches the original mountain site, not Tiller; the Tiller elevation is not in the sources read, so the field is flagged, not corrected. The record's 'None relocated' text should read as a 1985 relocation (added as an event). Access and hours should be checked before a visit: the FS and visitor hours differ, and the 2024 visitor noted the rangers may be moving to Canyonville.

Thin record: the four sources give the build year, owner and a 2022 condition report, but no fire history, no later repairs and no move or rental. Access is recorded as restricted because of gates on the BLM road and the uninhabitable building; no closure notice was found, so this is an inference. The brief's coordinates match the Register. The building is not recommended for entry.

Access level left unset: none of the four sources says whether the public may enter the tower, and the Register ties the site to an engine on high fire days. Total height not recorded: Forest Lookouts gives only the 20 ft ground-to-catwalk distance. The 1980s-to-2012 gap is undated in firelookout.com. The Roaming Civic and a Facebook group post describe the 1980s staffing history but were not read or cited. Register elevation 4,204 ft versus 4,200 ft elsewhere; not used in the story.

Main findings: the record's 6.1 m height is the earlier pole tower; the standing tower is 53 ft (about 16.2 m). The 1933 build year belongs to the first tower; the present R-6 tower dates from 1974. Build dates before 1933 vary across sources (1913, 1917, 1932). Story treats them as uncertain. The tower is condemned since 2016 and should not be climbed; the story does not encourage access. The 2022 Roaming Civic visit describes a climb, which the story does not repeat. Current agency, staffing and condition after 2022 are unconfirmed. Not read: the search snippet for a Sohs (research.sohs.org) article saying ODF has a 53-foot tower at the site today; it is a secondary search snippet and was not used as evidence. Oregon Hikers forum (2016) was not read. No photos added: the Roaming Civic 2022 photos are credited to a visitor and no URLs were captured. Forest Lookouts page credits photos to Rex Kamstra but no URLs were captured.

History rests on the NHLR detail page, firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill's November 2023 visit, and Forest Lookouts' extracts of Bend Bulletin items (quoted from newspapers, not checked against the scans). Build year: NHLR, Cheryl Hill and the Forest Lookouts summary give 1933; Forest Lookouts' note says construction in 1932. Elevation disagrees: NHLR 5,835 ft (1,779 m) against 5,900 ft on Cheryl Hill and firelookout.com. The record's 1778.5 m is left unchanged. Current staffing and access come from a 2023 visit and undated pages; no 2025 or 2026 source found, so recheck with the Bend-Fort Rock Ranger District before a visit. No rental listing found and none is claimed. No new photos added.

Core facts agree across sources: ODF-run, Jackson County, 1973 cab, unmanned since 2016 season, cameras since 2017. Early history conflicts: 1934 vs 1949-50 start, and 20 vs 24 feet. The brief's height_m 7.3 m is kept because it matches only the Weebly 24-foot figure. No fire is named. A 1995 Register-Guard profile quoted on the Weebly page reports a fire spotter's smoke sighting and grass fires called in (event 1995). A Former Fire Lookout Sites register page titled 'Round Top Lookout Site' appeared in a search snippet only (not read, not cited): it describes a 1933 crow's nest, a 1946 35-foot L-4 abandoned 1965 and removed 1970. It may be a different chronology for this peak. Worth a fetch and a county check before any edit. Access level 'public' refers to the site only; no source says the cab can be climbed.

Brief height_m 15.2 is the 1921 pole tower (50 ft), corrected to 25.0 m for the 82-foot tower. Access is marked closed for the tower; the road and trailhead are described as open in 2020 and 2023 accounts, but no official Forest Service notice was read. The 1941 Forest Lookouts date conflicts with 1949 sources. A Twin Lakes fire near-miss item seen in search results was not fetched and is not used. Staffing after 1964 not found. Newest status evidence is the 2023 visit.

Record height_m 3.0 looks wrong: the 1948 tower is 31'6" per the Register and Forest Lookouts (9.6 m); firelookout.com says 30 feet (9.1 m). Proposed 9.6 m is a correction for review, and facts.height_m uses it. Elevation: Register 6,154 ft (1,876 m) against 6,208 ft on firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill's list; the record's 1,875.7 m matches the Register and is kept. Name and spelling: the Register names William Parker as first lookout; Forest Lookouts quotes a 1915 item naming a Ray Parker; the Register's 1917 contractor (Mill-Made) and the newspaper quote (Mill-Maid) differ. Forest: the Register and firelookout.com say Rogue River National Forest; Cheryl Hill and the trip report say Rogue River-Siskiyou. The 2021 trip report is dated August 14, 2021 on the tag page; a March 2, 2025 date also appears beside it and was not checked further.
