Current staffing and access rest on a 2021 trip report and undated lists; no 2025 or 2026 source found, so recheck with the Butte Falls Ranger District. No photos added.

Current condition unknown: the latest source read is Cheryl Hill's July 2013 visit, which found the steel tower in place; no later report of the tower's condition or of the 1969 sale outcome was found. Do not treat it as standing today without a recent check. Record fixes: built 1922 is the crow's nest (proposed 1927); height_m 9.1 is 30 feet, the tree lookout (proposed 21.3 m for the 70-foot tower). Unresolved disagreements, not settled by the sources: tower height 60 feet (1926-27 Eugene paper) against 70 feet (Register, 1953 survey station, 1969 notices, Cheryl Hill); tower date 1926 (1927 newspaper 'last year') against 1927 (Register, firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill); elevation 4,940 ft (Register) against 4,969 ft (firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill, Forest Service); abandonment 1967 (firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill) against the 1969 notices, which say it 'no longer will be manned' in fire season. The Register's 'Built' field is not given; the 1927 date is taken from its description. Access: the Forest Service trail page gives the route as 1.1 miles along Road 142 to Road 144, then 0.8 mile to the end of Road 144, where the trail begins; the 1969 newspaper described a road stopping several hundred yards short, which may be a different route. No photos added.

The 1968 burning is consistent across sources; the build year (1930 to 1933) is contested and the record's 1932 is only firelookout.com's date. The only dated item is the Society page's 'As of 2025' road note, so the staffing as_of is that page's undated wording. Rental is listed by NHLR only; confirm with the Society before publishing rental details. Access level restricted because the spur road is gated 1.25 miles away. Not visited.

Brief's design 'D-6 cupola cabin' describes the older 1921 cabin, not the current tower; the current lookout is a flat-roof cab on a 40-foot steel tower (NHLR). Brief's height 9.1 m matches the 1962/63 wooden tower, so it is corrected to 12.2 m (40 ft, converted). Build year 2007 is consistent in the register but the Weebly listing says completed October 2007 and in service 2008. Sources disagree on the 1962/63 tower year and the 1914/1919/1921 early dates; the story reports the disagreement. 'Unmanned' and 'fenced' rest on a 2021 blog visit (as_of 2021-07), not a current official source. Access 'restricted' is inferred from the gate and fence. The 1931 Department of Commerce weather-cabin contract is in the Weebly listing but not footnoted in the story. Photos not added.

Brief's height_m 2.1 is wrong; 90 feet (27.4 m) is in the Register and FireLookout.com, so it is corrected. Build year conflict (1935 vs 1955) is real and unresolved; both are recorded. The 2007 fire entry is a threat, not a damage report, and comes from a history page quoting The Oregonian. The Oregonian article itself was not read. Access level 'permission' follows the Register's tribal-regulation line; the tribe's own visitor rules were not found. Staffing as_of 2026-07 is the Cherylhill directory date, and the FireLookout.com staffing text is undated.

Build year (about 1937 vs 1940) and removal year (1977 vs 1996) conflict; the 1992 survey is the best tiebreak but is not a Forest Service record. Access and visiting rules were not confirmed from a Forest Service page. No fire detections found. Trip-report pages seen only in search snippets (oregonhikers, cherylhill, oregonlookouts) were not read or cited. Quotes checked against the cached pages. Fact-check 2026-10-08: story reworded where it went beyond the sources ("first lookout", "today"); Clackamas County evidence added.

Brief listed 'built 1924' as the headline build event, but that appears to be the second (cabin) structure per firelookout.com, not the first (1910 tent camp) or the current (2004) building. NHLR's 1917 first-lookout date conflicts with firelookout.com's 1910 tent camp. Elevation in brief (1268.3m) matches NHLR's 4,161 ft / 1,268 m; recreation.gov states 4,223 ft, a minor discrepancy not resolved here. Fact-check 2026-10-04: story and evidence all checked out against source text; only fix was adding a missing footnote on the sentence naming the 15x15 cabin and the Gold Beach Ranger District (was previously uncited) and adding the footnote URL list, which the story file was missing entirely.

Brief height_m 61.0 is wrong; corrected to the 10-foot tower. Source 3 is a compiled history quoting newspapers and Forest Service files; all quotes were copied from its cached text. The 1930 cab type and the first cabin's date conflict between sources. Current access and visit details are thin: the only current sources are the staffed listing and the directory's legal-access column. The register's elevation differs from the directory's. The story gives no total height.

Brief height_m 30.2 is the planned 99-foot height from 1935, not the built height; corrected to 90 ft. The register's 80 ft is kept in the story. Status is standing but abandoned, with the last direct observation in May 2012; the 2026 directory is the only current source. Access is closed as of 2012 and not re-checked. The 2016 occupation is included only as a neutral event; the source is a compiled history page.

Current status rests on one 2023 blog visit and a BLM contact that the blogger reports; ODF did not reply to the blogger. The NHLR still says active service, and the brief's access 'unknown' is now recorded as closed on that basis. Elevation disagrees: NHLR 6,049 ft (1,844 m) matches the brief's 1843.7 m, while firelookout.com and the 2017 visit say 6,091 ft. Tower height disagrees (10 ft vs 9 ft 10 in after a 1993 raise). The closure date between 2017 and 2023 is unknown. No wildfire response, rental or Forest Service connection appears in these sources. An undated ODF Forest Log article on the Struck staffing was found but not used, because its date and quotes were not confirmed. No photos were added because no image URL with a licence was confirmed. Story is about 385 words.

Do not confuse with the South Baldy Lookout in the Colville and Kaniksu area of Washington (firelookout.com/wa/sbaldy.html; NHLR US register under /wa/). Access rests on one hobby site's 'No public access'; the register names ODF but gives no access rule. Verify with ODF before anyone plans a visit. Height is disputed (40 ft vs 50/54 ft). (2) The Former Fire Lookout Sites register carries a distinct, separate-looking listing, 'Escoheag Tower Site' (US 1585, RI 12), with coordinates about 0.4 miles from this tower's NHLR coordinates, but matching elevation, build year and agency -- almost certainly the same physical structure catalogued in both sister registers rather than a second nearby tower, but worth confirming. The brief's height 15.2 m is the 1917 wooden tower's height and is corrected to the current 65-foot steel tower. Staffing status 'unstaffed' rests on the register's Staffed? field alone. Two search results for Pine Hill (a directory listing for an address on Gardiner Rd, and a mapcarta entry) were not read and are not used.

Two sources agree on the 1935 build. Staffing, notable fires and any later condition work are not in the sources read. Providence Water pages at provwater.com and the Providence Journal Scituate article (2026-09-30) returned HTTP 403 and may hold more history. The register's 'active ever since' wording is general. Brief access 'unknown' is now resolved to permission-only by the NHLR text. No corrections to the brief.

NHLR gives only the 1930s for construction, so no built event is recorded. Staffing status none rests on the Forest Service statement that the tower is no longer in use and on NHLR standby status; the as_of date is the research date, and the staffing end (1993) is the last documented date. The county conflict is unresolved. No climbing information was found in the sources read, so visit.climbable is omitted. Hillmap and the OpenStreetMap node were checked but add no history. No new photos.

Build year (1938, CCC and WPA) and registration date (July 27, 2006) are from the NHLR entry alone. The brief's status 'standing' is not confirmed by any source read; the NHLR entry does not state current condition, so facts.status is omitted. No staffing or fire history was found, so no staffing facts or fire events are recorded. Tower-specific access and climbing rules were not found; the access level 'public' reflects the open university forest with trail rules, not a statement about the tower. The Clemson World items concern the Lake Issaqueena recreation area, not the tower, and are used as context only. The 'other' event for 1934 is the WPA land program, not a tower event. The brief's coordinates match the NHLR coordinates. No new photos.

Brief said built 1936; NHLR gives circa 1936-1938, so the event year is the low end of that range. 'Possibly a Bethlehem Steel model' is NHLR's own hedge. The 1993 abandonment is one NHLR statement, backed by the statewide SCFC closure date; the staffing 'unstaffed as of 1993' is inferred from those two, not from a staffing record. No access or visit data was found, so the access and visit keys are omitted. The eastern lookouts page and the hillmap and OpenStreetMap pages add only name, county and agency, so they are not cited. Used 3 web searches, one over the 2-search budget. No fire history, newspaper coverage or NRHP listing was found.

Brief's facts hold up: 1965 build, 22 ft (6.7 m), standing. The 1964 authorization and the 1965 contract come from a newspaper item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, not from the newspapers themselves. Staffing is unknown; a search turned up no staffing or fire history. Tower-specific access is not stated: the SummitPost guide covers the surrounding game production area only, so no access level is recorded. The NHLR says the land is managed by the state fish and game department, while the brief lists the agency as the state forestry department; both are recorded. Used 2 web searches, within budget. No photos were added. Two photo credits exist on the NHLR and Rex's pages (Ron Kemnow; Dave Masters), but no image URLs were captured, so none are listed.

The 1939 steel tower and L-4 cab are supported by at least two sources (register and firelookout.com) and the Forest Service. The 1910 first tower rests on the Forest Service page alone; a 1915 newspaper item shows a lookout station by then. Access 'public' is an inference from the register's road note and the Forest Service description of recreationist use; the Forest Service page is undated and nothing says whether the cab may be climbed. Height 9.1 m converts the 30-ft figure.

Rapid City Journal rename article returned HTTP 429 on this pass; not used. Height_m 11.0 and precise elevation carried from the existing record, not independently re-confirmed by a new source this round.

Brochure PDF text extraction was garbled/reflowed in places (OCR-like layout artifacts); only the clearly legible fragments were used. Could not independently verify current rental/visitation status beyond 'public' access level from the existing record.

Two register claims (CCC build in 1941, cabin burned in the late 1990s) conflict with other sources and are reported as disputed. Current staffing comes from an undated Forest Service page. The Aermotor attribution rests on firelookout.com alone. Access 'public' follows the Forest Service page, which describes visitor climbs in the staffed season; drive-up is not described.

Build year of the current stone tower is disputed between 1939 (NHLR, Parkwolf) and 1940-41 (FFLA); a 1939 newspaper excerpt describing a log tower adds ambiguity. Height given in the brief (15.2 m) likely refers to the tower structure; elevation sources consistently give the peak as 6,023 ft, slightly different from the brief's 6,003 ft NHLR figure -- flagged as a minor discrepancy, not corrected since NHLR is the brief's own source.

Strongest sources are the NPS Wind Cave assessment (npshistory.com PDF) for construction, use and 1998 access change, and the NPS trail page for current climbing rules. The 1954 newspaper quoted on westlookouts calls the Rankin Ridge watcher a State Park lookout, which does not fit the national park; the story avoids naming that person. No rental or staffing information after 1998 was found; access is recorded as closed to climbing, with the trail open. The NHLR CL100 design label and the NPS 'Standard Steel Lookout Tower' proposal are not in conflict, but only the register gives the CL100 name.

The 1966 versus 1975 steel-tower date is the main open question; a Black Hills National Forest history or a Forest Service lookout inventory would settle it. Current access rests on one hiking blog of unknown date plus a SummitPost route description; no Forest Service page for this tower was found, and the Black Hills NF page checked says five towers remain in service without naming them. No rental listing found. The brief's height_m (16.2) was left out of facts because sources conflict.

Build-date conflict across four sources (1935/1939/1939-40/1942) could not be fully resolved within the research budget; flagged in both story and corrections. Worth a closer look at NRHP/npgallery nomination documents if available, which might clarify construction vs completion dates.

No register page exists for Avondale on nhlr.org or firetower.org (checked cached TN listings for both; it isn't there), no NRHP nomination, no newspaper hit, and no mention in a general East Tennessee fire-tower news piece that was checked. Web search surfaced an AI-synthesized claim that Avondale is 'also known as Clinch Lookout Tower,' but no primary source for that name turned up (anyplaceamerica.com, the likely origin, returned 403) so it was left out rather than guessed into the story. Builder, year built, agency, staffing and access all remain unknown; a human with access to TN Division of Forestry records or local Grainger County history might find more.

Current access level in the brief was 'unknown'; set to restricted based on NRHP note that the cab was locked during survey and the tower is an active state asset rather than a public rental. No conflicting build years found for this tower. Fact-check 2026-10-04: removed an unsupported '2017' NRHP-listing year (not stated by any cited source; the NRHP form's bibliography has a 2017 website-access date that appears to have been mistaken for the listing year) and corrected the footnote on the Clear Fork/New Rivers location detail, which is sourced to [3] (Encyclopedia of Scott County), not [1] (NHLR) alone.

No source found for the year the tower moved to air-quality use, or for any fire-lookout staffing history. Height: the register and the hiking guide say 60 feet; an NPS profile describes the top as 80 feet in the air. Not reconciled; height_m uses the 60-ft figure. The access statement comes from an undated hiking guide, not an NPS notice, so check with the NPS before publishing. The register also lists Smoky Mountain Hiking Club and Friends of the Great Smoky Mountains as cooperators; not used. A Wikidata entry gives inception 1935; not used.

No construction date found; the register gives no build year and the 1942 photograph is the earliest dated evidence. Access and staffing come from a March 2006 visit report, nearly 20 years old; 'closed' is an inference from the removed stairs and posted signs and should be checked. Do not merge with the Central US Lookouts 'Flatwoods' page: a search snippet describes a different CCC tower near Greenville Camp on Highway 67, which is not this one. The OSM record (lattice tower, 291 m) is not used.

The Mississippi origin and the 1943 move rest on the NHLR register. The Komoot guide repeats both and may have taken them from the register, so they are not independent confirmations. No source dates the wooden predecessor; 1934 is inferred from 'nine years earlier'. Current status is unclear: the last visit report is June 2004 (cab torn off), TN Landforms says standing, and Wikipedia says dismantled with a communications tower. Access level 'restricted' is our reading of the register's emergency-only use and the guide's 'cannot be climbed'; no official access notice was found. The 100-ft figure is the register's tower height and is not confirmed as height to the cab floor, so height_m is omitted.

Build year is the one real conflict. The register says 1948, while the NRHP nomination and Clio say 1936 and the 1933 newspaper item shows it was planned earlier; a correction to 1936 is proposed for human review. Staffing is not recorded: the register's visit page reads 'Staffed? No', but that line is split and was not quoted. The NRHP period of significance ends in 1965, while Clio says the Tennessee Division of Forestry used it until the mid-1970s; the two describe different things and both are noted. The register names the Tennessee Division of Forestry as administrator, but the nomination places the tower inside Cherokee National Forest on Fire Tower Road. The register gives 3,885 feet while the NRHP nomination gives 3,889. The NRHP gives 60 feet. Clio says trail and tower repair plans were in the works, so current conditions may have changed since the 2021 visit. The register's 1948 may come from a later rebuild or a transcription error; the sources read do not say which.

The 1957 build date rests on the NRHP nomination, which cites a 2014 personal communication with the Division's fire management leader; the NHLR entry says build date unknown. Listing date: the nomination gives 11/14/2017; search snippets (TreeAlive, Register Atlas) give Nov 16, 2017; neither was fetched, so the story says only November 2017. Elevation disagrees: 627 ft (NRHP; 191.1 m in the cached tnlandforms GPX) vs 613 ft / 187 m (NHLR); the record's 186.8 m matches the NHLR. The 80-ft height is the overall structure height per the NRHP and NHLR; not confirmed as cab-floor height. The access level 'restricted' is the researcher's reading of 'active TN Forestry site'; no source states public access, so the editor should confirm. The Courier Winter 2018 article (TN Historical Commission) could not be fetched (connection reset). The staffing end date is 'mid-1970s' with no exact year.

Facts are thin: no construction year, staffing history, or access status surfaced within budget. A linked 1955 photo citation (tnsos.org/tsla imagesearch, ImageID=15168) returned HTTP 403 and could not be read; it may be worth a human follow-up for a caption or date. No newspaper or NRHP material found for this specific tower. Fact-check 2026-10-04: removed two overclaims not supported by their cited quotes - the story had attributed the 1955 photo to the Tennessee State Library and Archives (the tnlandforms source only says "1955 photo", with no holding institution named) and had the November 2023 site visit "find the tower still intact" (the register entry is just "Site Visit - 11/25/23", with no stated outcome). Both fixed to state only what the sources say.

No source read gives a build year for the block tower. Search snippets (Pinterest, Tripadvisor) say 1950s and 'since 1926' but were not fetched and are not cited. The 2013 conversion date rests on one source (Eastern US lookouts). The 2017 blog does not give a year. Access 'public' rests on a user-submitted travel listing and the Eastern US lookouts site's 'for public use'; the 2008 visit sheet shows no signs. Please confirm current access with the Cherokee National Forest before publishing. The NHLR's description still reads as a block tower and may be out of date. The tnlandforms GPX (cached) lists the site as 'Cocke cnf standing'; it is not cited because the GPX is not a readable page. The record's material 'masonry' comes from the NHLR and may be out of date after the 2013 conversion; no correction was proposed for material.

The brief's 2023 restoration (A Forever Places crew) and the 1995 'work finished a few years later' are not in any page I read, so they are left out. The Mountain Press restoration article returned HTTP 429 and was not read. Staffing years and any fires the tower spotted are not in these sources. Access is rated public as a hiking destination; climbing rules were not verified. A tnlandforms listing puts the peak in Haywood County, NC, which conflicts with the register's Cocke County, TN; the story does not mention a county. Used 1 WebSearch call and 6 page reads (one returned HTTP 429).

Build date and builder are unresolved: the register says 1930 and the wiki credits the Civil Conservation Corps without a date. The CCC was set up in 1933 (not sourced here), so either the 1930 date or the builder credit needs checking against a Cherokee National Forest history or the Forest Service's own tower file. Access is public per the Forest Service pages, but the 2008 register visit is the only condition report; the 2011 restoration has no later condition report. The NHLR text about restoration is undated, so the story relies on the Forest Service date for 2011.

Brief's built year 1964 is a misreading of NHLR ('after 1964'); corrected to 1970 from TDF files. Brief's elevation (158.5 m) and 1 Jan 2023 registration match NHLR. Added height 80 ft = 24.4 m from NHLR. Staffing unknown; no staffing or fire history found. No access or visit data: NHLR calls the site an active TN Forestry location, which is not a public-access statement, so no access level is recorded. The NRHP listing date comes from Wikipedia (which cites AP) and the heritageindex/Aubrey pages; the NPGallery record for 100004684 was not readable. tnlandforms rows are laid out in columns; the standing status is read from the 'Ripley 521 Lauderdale 9-14 standing' row, which the same site's GPX file also shows. Used 2 web searches, within budget. No photos added; NHLR has photos but no image URLs were captured.

Build date, design type and elevation conflict between the register and the NRHP nomination; both kept in the story. Current access and staffing rest on the nomination's 2014-era information, not a current site visit or Division of Forestry notice. The NRHP listing date was not confirmed from the sources read (NPGallery shows only a published date of 3/31/2015), so no nrhp_listed event was entered. No notable fires named in sources. No rental listing found. The record's 1933 'built' is kept; the 1934 completion is added as its own event.

Thin record. The register gives only 'late 1950s' for construction, so no built event was written. The brief's 2019 NHLR registration was not seen in the pages read, so it is not cited. Topozone (search snippet only, not read) places the tower on an 'Evensville' USGS map, a possible place-name variant. A 2015 TDF tower history report (search snippet only, not read) probably gives the exact build year. The NRHP study's county table appears to list a Smyrna entry in Rhea County (table layout not quoted). Staffing and any status after 2019 are unknown. Page reads for this tower reached the six-read budget.

Build date, builder, staffing and fire history are not in the NHLR entry, the Forest Lookouts listing or the tnlandforms inventory. Two web searches returned only statewide background (CCC tower counts, a 2015 Division report title) that is not cited. Aermotor is hedged by the register ('believed'). The access sign comes from a register entry of about 2018-2019; verify on site or with the Division before publishing. Record fields design and height_m are still null; design is filled here from the register.

No build date, builder or designing agency found in the sources read (NHLR detail page has no Built field). The agency is not established: the 2006 visit notes a TN Dept of Forestry sign and locked shed on site, but no administration statement was found, so no agency fact is recorded. The only physical description is a 2006 visit report; the Tennessee Landforms list (undated snapshot) shows it standing. Access was inferred from the fence and no-trespassing signs in that 2006 report, so the level is restricted pending a current source. The 100-ft height is the visit report's figure, converted to 30.5 m. OpenStreetMap tags it tower:construction=lattice; not used because it is user-edited and does not give a date.

No source beyond tnlandforms.us mentions this specific tower by name; the register has no build year, design, agency confirmation beyond the district-tower numbering convention, staffing, or access information. Checked nhlr.org and firetower.org (FFLOS) crawl caches for Tennessee and the local raw-page caches for 'white house'/'whitehouse' — none has an entry for this tower. Two WebSearches turned up nothing tower-specific beyond tnlandforms.us. The 'agency' fact: fact-check spot-checking (2026-10-04) found the source page does directly name 'Tennessee Division of Forestry (208 tower sites c. 1976...)' alongside the district-tower numbering explanation, so this is a direct naming rather than an inference as originally noted. No corrections to the tower record are warranted — tnlandforms is already the record's source for name/location/county/elevation/status.

Build years 1961-1962 and the Aermotor belief rest on the register entry alone; no second source was found. The Luminary name is unexplained in all sources read. A social media search result called the site abandoned; it is unreliable, was not read at source, and is left out. Access is not established. The state-forest rule applies only if the tower is on state forest land, which is not confirmed. Record fields design and access are unfilled; design is filled here from the register.

NHLR (decommissioned 1970) and Texas Escapes (functioned into the 1980s) disagree on when the tower stopped operating; noted in the story rather than resolved. The on-site historical marker (hmdb.org #31698) returned HTTP 403 and could not be read, so its exact inscription is not cited here. Texas Escapes is a general-interest history site, not a primary source, so the Wesley Love / WPA narrative rests on that one article; a Texas Historical Commission marker file or a Jacksonville Daily Progress archive piece would strengthen it. A draft citation to 'Forest Fire Lookout Association (firelookout.org)' claiming its Texas lookouts list records this tower as standing has been removed: the cached source is actually the Former Fire Lookout Sites register (firetower.org, a sister site of NHLR, not FFLA), it catalogs decommissioned/removed lookouts, and its one Texas entry is Jefferson Lookout Site, not Love's Lookout. The source neither supports the claim nor matches the cited publisher, so both the footnote and the sentence were dropped.

Very thin record. Smith Ferry is not registered in the cached National Historic Lookout Register or FFLOS listings for Texas, and no construction date, design, height, staffing, or fate (standing/removed/burned) beyond the FFLA list's bare 'Standing' turned up in two web searches plus the cached regional lookout lists. The Texas Escapes citation is general East Texas context (phase-out to aerial patrol), not Smith-Ferry-specific; flagged as such in the story. Worth a follow-up with Texas A&M Forest Service records or Tyler County historical sources if a human researcher has more time/budget.

No newspaper, NRHP, or forest-history coverage found specific to this tower; it is recent (built 2023, NHLR-registered Jan 2026) so that may simply not exist yet. The NHLR nominator, Alfred Francis Gessel, shares a surname with a contact address once suspected on the Timber Lane Utility District site, raising a guess that he may be a district official involved in bringing the tower to the park — but this was never sourced (the district-facilities page carries no contact names or emails) and has been dropped from the story entirely rather than left as insinuation. Climbability and drive-up access are unconfirmed; the park's own page references a 'Fire Tower Flyer' that was not reachable in this research. One correction applied: the NHLR elevation figure (113 ft / 34 m) is not labeled by the register as site elevation vs. structure height, so the story no longer asserts which it is. The district-facilities source was dropped (it supported neither the Fire Tower Flyer mention, which is on the parks-and-trails page, nor the contact-name claim, which isn't on the site at all); the FFLA citation is renumbered [^3] accordingly.

Two small date conflicts in the sources, both noted in the story rather than resolved: last staffed year (NHLR: 1968; Deseret News: 1969) and the restoration year before the 2008 closure (NHLR: 1986; Deseret News: early-1980s renovation, reopened 1987). Nothing in hand to adjudicate either. The record itself checks out against all sources on name, location, build year (1937) and status. The tower is now a staffed-by-volunteers interpretive/tour site rather than an active detection post, which the current record's staffing/access/visit fields didn't yet reflect. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04) found a third, previously unflagged conflict: NHLR gives elevation as 8,819 ft, but Wikipedia, Wikidata and willhiteweb all give 8,834 ft; now flagged in the story and as a correction above rather than resolved. Also corrected three footnote misattributions in the original story/JSON draft: the '360 square miles' view figure and the above-ground-living-quarters uniqueness claim were cited partly to NHLR, which does not state either; and the NRHP listing date/reference number was cited partly to NHLR, which gives only the 1978 nomination, not the 1980 listing date or reference number. Willhiteweb separately gives a 1935 build year, at odds with the 1937 given by NHLR, Wikipedia, Wikidata and Deseret News; left unflagged since the story never cites willhiteweb for the build year and the other four sources agree. Also fixed a pronoun error: the story referred to the current volunteer tour guide as 'him', but the cited Deseret News source names her as Clare Boerigter ('her third season').

Do not use fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/high-knob-tower for this record: that page describes the High Knob Tower in the Clinch Ranger District (Wise County, VA), a different tower with a 2014 rebuild. The GWNF High Knob is in Rockingham County, VA. Staffing is recorded as unknown because the sources read do not say when the tower last had a lookout. Interior access is recorded as restricted based on the 2018 NHLR visit comment, which is not an official closure notice; a current check with the George Washington and Jefferson National Forests is advised. Trail details come from the Visit Harrisonburg guide (2025 PDF).

The record name 'moved from its original spot' is not supported by the cited sources, which describe dismantling and reinstallation on Jack Mountain. The coordinates differ: the record's tower point (38.395783, -79.563883) and the separate FFLA 'Sounding Knob' point (38.34636, -79.59001) are about 6 km apart by my estimate. No source explains that gap, so it needs checking. A Highland County Chamber of Commerce directory lists 'Sounding Knob Fire Tower (Firetower LLC)', which suggests a business operator. I saw only a search snippet, so ownership and access may have changed since 2021. Elevation 1214 m is kept from the brief, not re-checked. Staffing 'until the 1960s' is a decade only, so no event year is given. Read budget: five distinct pages and two searches, close to the cap.

Elevation differs: NHLR gives 3,304 ft (1,007 m), which the record and story use; Wikipedia gives 3315 ft for the same peak. Not reconciled. Build history: the NHLR detail page gives no build year. Forest Lookouts, quoting a 1921 state report, has a tower and telephone line on Westmore Mountain that year, and a new steel tower built by the New England Forest Emergency fund in work dated 1938-40. Whether the standing tower is the 1938-40 steel tower, or whether the 1921 tower was replaced, is not stated in any source read. The NorthWoods Stewardship Center page cited by the 2013 and 2024 chapter reports returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The Ranger's Cabin (2013 report), the summit cabin (2002 and 2016 reports, 2025 roof) may be the same building; sources read do not say. 2016 condition conflict: the NHLR visit report of August 21, 2016 describes cab graffiti, bullet holes and a portion of the roof blown off, while the chapter's October 2016 hike found the tower and summit cabin in good shape. Roof: the 2008, 2010 and 2012 chapter reports call for repair or replacement; the 2022 report says replaced 'last year', read as 2021, which is an inference. Agency: Wikipedia says the forest is managed by Vermont DFPR; the 2022 chapter report calls the tower state-owned. The tower's own managing agency is not named in the sources read. Access: signed route from the 2016 NHLR visit report and the 2025 report are the newest; no current closure, staffing or booking notice was read. Staffing: the NHLR visit report has a Staffed? question; not used as a fact. Budget: four fetch_text page reads (NHLR, Forest Lookouts, the 2025 chapter report, Wikipedia) plus one blocked NorthWoods page; two WebSearch calls; the other chapter reports were read from the local cache with pdftotext -layout. No new photos added; the record photo is from the NHLR (Jack Kelley, all rights reserved).

Brief's 2007 'concrete steps repaired, no cab or tower work' event is not included. It appears only in a search snippet from cr-vt-2007.pdf (firelookout.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/cr-vt-2007.pdf), which was not read, so it is unverified here; worth a fetch and a quote. The 2025 MyChamplainValley closure notice is posted May 2, 2025, so the closure is now dated and used in the story. The register's 'open to the public' line is undated. Burke 54 ft matches brief height_m 16.5. Brief elevation_m 981.5 matches the register's 3,220 ft (981 m). Brief access 'unknown' is now public per the register. The Burlington Free Press 2025 article returned HTTP 403. Read budget used: 6 successful page reads plus one 403.

Brief lat/lon 44.5287, -72.544517 is the register's point. The FFLA list gives 44.52639, -72.54603, roughly 250 m apart. UVM text says the summit is 795 feet, which looks like a units slip; Wikipedia gives 795 m. Height 13.9 m is converted from the 1938-40 report's 45 ft 9 in. Brief 'Lemoille' county is a misspelling; correction proposed. Not searched: a snippet says the tower is decommissioned but still standing (not read). Page reads: 4 new (Wikipedia, UVM, NHLR, Forest Lookouts); FFLA list and 2025 PDF reused from earlier fetches. Staffing after 1974 not found.

The closure dates conflict (2022 Vermont report vs April 22, 2025 Forest Service alert), so the closure is stated as current but its start is left open. The July 2026 status comes from a single personal hiking blog; check the Forest Service alert before publishing. Leads not read: a Green Mountain Club alert saying repair funding is being sought, and a federal contract for structural repairs to the Glastenbury and Stratton towers; both could change access. The Appalachian Trail Conservancy page has a 04/23/2025 update saying the tower remains closed; not read. The 'owned by Green Mountain Forest' wording in the 2022 report looks like a shorthand for the national forest. Used 1 WebSearch and 6 page reads.

Brief check: 'still closed in the 2021 report' is verified (cr-vt-2021.pdf: 'continues to remain Closed'). Access changes from the brief's 'unknown' to 'closed'. Gaps: (1) No staffing years anywhere in the sources read; the NHLR 'about a decade' is the only statement, so no staffed or staffed_last event is recorded. (2) Current status after the 2021 report is unknown; no reopening is shown but none is ruled out. (3) The Valley News column is undated in the copy read; 'about 10 years back' for the NorthWoods work is relative to an unknown date, so no year is given for it. (4) The column says 'It was sold to a paper company in 1961' right after describing the warden's cabin. The antecedent of 'It' is ambiguous (cabin or tower or land), so the story leaves that sentence out. (6) A search snippet quoting a NorthWoods trail director about summit cabins being removed or burned was not from a page read, so it is not used. (7) Do not confuse this with New Hampshire's Mount Monadnock. (8) TPL spells the mountain 'Monandnock'; the quotes use the NHLR spelling. (9) NHLR photos are credited to Craig Hamelin; no image URLs were added. Budget: 6 distinct pages read (one, the easternuslookouts.weebly.com Monadnock page, returned only navigation and is not cited) and 1 WebSearch.

Brief events for 2013 (footing repairs), 2014 (FFLA grant), and 2018 (glass removed; steel stairs) were not confirmed in the sources read and are left out of the story. The 2016 Register visit reports most of the cab glass already missing, which sits awkwardly with a 2018 glass-removal date. The FPR park page is undated, so the mid-December closure cannot be dated; do not treat it as current without checking. The Forest Lookouts history gives the wooden tower 30 ft in 1949 and 40 ft in 1935; the NGS 1942 survey describes a wooden tower about 60 ft tall on Hogback Mountain, which may be a different structure. Brief's 2010 're-wooded' wording is not in the register text read (corrected). Not verified in pages read: the 2012 'ski area workers' and certificate detail, and the June 19, 2023 NHLR registration date (the grep did not return the date line), so neither is in the story. Pages read: 8, over the 6-page budget because the NHLR and Eastern pages are long.

Two open conflicts are reported in the story: the move year (1943 vs 1944) and the 1931 tower design. The brief's height_m 24.0 is not supported by any page read, so it is left out of facts; no source found gives the steel tower's height. The Register lists the summit site at 2,947 ft while the state page gives 3,037 ft. No photos added. Forest Lookouts page also holds 1938 and 1947-1957 maintenance notes, not used.

Several sources disagree on dates and heights (see resolved_conflicts). The 'today' access rests on an undated USFS trail page. The NRHP nomination is dated March 1990 (Hugh H. Henry), before the 1992 listing. Current condition is unconfirmed: the newest status line is the 2015 register entry. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04) found the original story had miscited and conflated two of its numbers. (1) The 'five miles northwest of Yelm' location sentence was footnoted to the register (firetower.org), which actually says only 'Olympia, Thurston County' and never mentions Yelm; the Yelm distance comes from firelookout.com instead, so the footnote has been corrected to cite that source. (2) The steel tower's '118 ft' figure, footnoted as the IslandWood rebuilder's figure for the *same 1968 tower* the register puts at 112 ft, is actually that source's figure for the *rebuilt* Canopy Tower as it stands today at IslandWood -- and that source gives two different figures for that rebuilt height (125 ft and 118 ft) in two different places on its own page. The rebuilder's page gives no height at all for the original Fort Lewis tower, and separately dates its construction to 1966, not 1968 (a discrepancy the original story missed entirely). The story and this record have been corrected to state these distinctions rather than conflating them. Also fixed: the rebuilding firm was called 'Sahale Snowkites & Climbing' in the original story and source list -- that name does not appear anywhere on the cited page, which identifies the firm as 'Sahale LLC' (operating as Seattle Bridge Builders LLC); corrected throughout. The decommission-year disagreement (2000 vs 1998) and the general staffing/fire-history gap were both verified as accurately described in the original story and have been left as-is, with firelookout.com's agreement with the register's 2000 date now also cited. No staffing, named lookouts (other than 2010 FFLOS nominator Irene Potter), or fire-detection history for the Rainier site turned up in any cached or web source -- this appears to be a genuine gap in the record, not a search failure. The sibling record us-wa-rainier-lookout-site-at-islandwood gives height_m as 125.0, which is almost certainly a feet-to-meters unit mixup (125 ft, not 125 m, matching the 125 ft figure found on the rebuilder's own page) rather than meters; worth a human look at that record, though it is outside the scope of this task to edit it.

Height: record 4.0 m is unsupported; sources give a 10-ft tower (proposed 3.0 m). The record's 1910 'built' event is the first cab; the present tower (1959) is added as its own event. Dates for the first cab (1910 vs 1913) and the restoration crews (2007-08 vs 2010) conflict; both are reported. Access is marked restricted because the road is gated and no source documents public entry to the cab. All source pages are undated except the 2010 PCT quote. PCT Washington's 1913 first-cab date and 1938 garage date were added on this check. The WTA route is 3.1 miles plus 0.3 mile to the gated road (about 3.4 miles), and the story now ends that figure at the gate. No climbing advice is given.

Dates are the hardest part of this record. Willhite Web and TrailChick are personal trip-report sites, used for dates and access details only. The Washington Lookouts page is a secondary compilation; the 1918 and 1926 items are quoted from it. Several local pages list the same site under the name Red Top Mountain.

Build year disagrees: 1964 in the register, firelookout and TrailChick, 1965 in the 2018 tDAR study; story states both. Record height_m 10.7 looks like the 1927 pole tower (35 ft); facts.height_m set to 3.0 for the present 10-foot tower, please confirm the cab-floor height. The 2018 visit report on the register says Staffed? No, and the 2018 TrailChick visit says last staffed 1976; no later staffing source found. No current rental or open-to-visitors information found; the 2022 Forest Service project page does not say the cab is open. Staffing rests on the 2024 TrailChick page and an undated firelookout.com page; no 2025 or 2026 source was confirmed. The 2019 tours come from TrailChick only. No source gave an exact trail name/mileage within budget; left access as general trail note rather than inventing specifics. No distinct fire events found tied to this lookout specifically.

Fact-check 2026-10-04: removed several story sentences that went beyond the cited source (an invented etymology for the 'Skyline' name, a claim the design was 'widely used' by the state forestry service, invented reasoning about dry grass/wind/debris burning driving spring staffing, and an invented claim that decommissioning was 'in favor of aircraft and other detection methods') — none of this appears in the NHLR page text. Also note cite 2's FFLA list spells the feature 'Friendship Mound (Skyline)', slightly differing from cite 1's 'Friendship (Skyline)'; not treated as a correction since both clearly refer to the same tower.

The register is the only source for the first site (about 736 ft) and the later move; no other source I read mentions a move, so that claim is single-sourced. The record's agency is the former operator (WI DNR); the current owner is the Friends of the Bird Sanctuary per the 2021 news report, and the record's ownership 'unknown' could be updated, but no correction is proposed because the record does not claim an owner. The 2015 decommissioning and 2017 NHLR registration match the record. Staffing and climb schedule details come from 2021-2022 reports and may have changed; the 2026 status of the open-climb schedule was not checked. The Airbnb listing was not read directly (JavaScript-heavy), so the rental is supported only by the 2021 article and the FFLA rentals list. Four web reads, one WebSearch (the second was not needed).

The 1934 date is an upper bound (in place by 1934), not a known construction date; the brief's 'built 1934' should be read that way. Not found: current staffing by the Tribe, any tribal statement on the tower, or visitor information. Access is private property, so the story advises permission only.

Brief's 1932 build is supported by the 2008 nomination (prefab 1932, pier dated 10/22/32 at the original site); the 1935 date in the Forest Service page and Wikipedia is the relocation year. Brief record lacked the 1935 relocation and the 2008 NRHP event, both added. Access and seasons come from the Forest Service page; staffing from the NHLR 'Staffed? No' field and the nomination's 1960s end of use. NHLR gives no Built field. One WebSearch via websearch.py; about six page reads including the nomination PDF (one GetAsset ID returned no text). No photos added.

Thin record. The Register entry is the only detailed source; the 1946 photograph record is the only staffing evidence. The WJFW feature covers Wisconsin towers in general and does not name Rock Falls, so its 2015 decommissioning is not applied here. No source on current access, condition or climbing; the record keeps access unknown. The Register's 100-foot figure is the tower's stated height, not measured to the cab floor, so it is not in height_m. Record location, elevation (508 m), county and agency agree with the sources. No corrections proposed. The Forest Lookouts Rock Falls page has a header and navigation only. No new photos with image URLs were found; the photograph record is cited as a source, not as an image.

Sources conflict on the build date (Register: early 1930s; Forest Lookouts: a 1923 53-foot Blaw-Knox tower and a February 1930 'new steel fire tower') and on height (47 vs 53 feet). The story says so and does not pick one. Unresolved: whether the 1923 structure is the tower standing today. Current condition is unknown: the 2021 article says a contractor was to start repairs that summer, and the HawkinsRails page is undated and says the summit tower was abandoned; neither is a current report. The Register's visit and access details are not in the record. The cabin rental is supported only by the June 2021 article; check current booking before publishing. The record has no built year; none is proposed as a correction. No corrections proposed. Not verified on site.

Build date (circa 1926) rests on NHLR and one 1926 newspaper item; Wikipedia's 1939 is a weaker later bound. Condition is from a single 2017 NHLR visit and Wikipedia's 2016 status. The repeater project was approved in 2010 and the tower was not removed (Wikipedia). The Reddit and FFLA items were not used: a 1988 transfer to the Forest Service is unverified. Access: hiking via a gate and 3/4-mile walk; no climbing.

The 1931 build and 1943 move agree across the Register, the Dolly Sods site record and the Forest Service history, so the history is well supported. Height is unresolved: 30-foot legs (Register) against about 70 feet (1956 station description quoted on the Forest Lookouts page); the record's 3.0 m matches neither, and the proposed 9.1 m is from the Register's legs and needs a human check. The cab collapse year is 2010 in two sources and before October 2015 in the Register. Current condition rests on the 2020 Register visit report and a 2013 travel post; not checked on site. Access (grassy road off Forest Road 19) comes from the 2013 travel post only. The Reddit and abandonedonline pages were not used. Nothing in the 1976 newspaper item was used beyond the employee's remark. No new photos with image URLs were added.

Construction date and design are well supported by the register and a local site. Current condition rests on the 2021 register visit; no 2025-2026 report was found. Staffing history not found; the register's staffed field is blank. Hike length conflicts (2.6 vs 4 miles). A YouTube search snippet describes the tower as 60 ft (Aermotor MC-39); the fetched page had no description text, so this is not used. The Lost River State Park Wikipedia page does not mention the tower. No photos added; licenses not checked. Read budget ran about two pages over the cap.

Current closure and rebuild plan are well documented (Gazette-Mail 2024, RealWV 2026, volunteer site). The history is less certain: the register's Built field (1997) contradicts its own description (1934), and rebuild dates differ across three sources. The 2020 report names the FFLA in its own title, so the publisher credit is no longer inferred. Elevation differs between the register and Gazette-Mail. Register photos (credited to Brian Powell and Victoria Oliver) were not added; licences not checked. The RealWV figure of $130,000 in donations was not used. The trail length (about one mile) is from RealWV and the Gazette-Mail (a mile-long trek); the Gazette-Mail's wording was not used for access. Read budget ran to about six page reads plus one search.

Built date (1963, Backbone 1922) and elevation agree across the Forest Service, NHLR and Wikipedia. Current condition rests on one undated NHLR visit report. The register's staffing field has mixed visit answers ('No' on one visit, 'Sometimes' on a July 31, 2019 visit); both are now quoted and reported in the story. Access comes from the Forest Service page. One WebSearch via websearch.py; four page reads. No photos. No rental listed for Olson in the sources read.

Build year conflicts: the NHLR says 1925 (WV Conservation Commission); the 1973 Charleston Gazette, quoted by Forest Lookouts, says the tower was originally built to 60 feet in 1927. Both kept as events. Elevation conflicts: NHLR 3,364 ft (matches record elevation_m 1025.3); the 1973 article says 3,500 ft; the 1916 report quoted by Forest Lookouts says 3,550 ft. Not reconciled. Record height_m 30.5 matches the NHLR's 100-foot total height, so it is kept. Registration correction: FFLOS US 1692 ('Potato Hill Tower Site', registered 2017) gives its location as unknown in Webster County with coordinates unlisted, and Forest Lookouts uses the name Potato Hill as a historic name for this site. Whether the FFLOS tower is this one is not established; the correction proposes unlinking, and the 2017 fflos_registered event was left out of this tower's events for that reason. Access and current condition: the newest sources are the NHLR (undated) and the firelookout.org list; the NHLR links to a 2015 video of a climb; no source read says whether the public may visit or climb now. Searches found no 2024-2025 access notice. The WBOY article on climbable WV towers does not mention Point Mountain. Ownership: the NHLR names the WV Division of Forestry as administrator; the Monongahela National Forest list in a search summary was not read and was not used. Budget: four fetch_text page reads (NHLR, FFLOS, firelookout WV list, WBOY), one failed fetch of a WV tower list PDF (DNS error), two WebSearch calls, and one local read of the cached Forest Lookouts page (eastern_us_lookouts/point-mountain.html). No photos added.

Build date 'by 1925' comes from the FFLOS Randolph County record; NHLR's Built 1999 is the relocation year. The record's events list 1999 as built and should be corrected. A WBOY search snippet places the tower 'on top of Cheat Ridge' in Pocahontas County; the page was not read, so the Snowshoe Mountain location rests on NHLR. The 80-foot height is from one history page only. Access: private resort ground; no climbing.

The NHLR says originally built in the 1920s by the CCC; the state history credits the Civilian Conservation Corps with forest work but places a 1924 tower on Michael Mountain. Search snippets from theclio.com/entry/45123 and wvencyclopedia.org credit the CCC with building the 1935 tower, but those pages were not opened and no quote was recorded. Read on the 2026-10-08 fact-check, easternuslookouts.weebly.com/thorny-mountain.html (not cited in the story, not an NHLR or state source): a '1935' entry says the lookout duties were transferred to this site from Michael Mountain, which bears on the 'Michael Mountain link is not confirmed' sentence; a November 28, 1937 Bluefield Daily Telegraph item says a new tower with observer's cabin atop a '40-foot steel framework' was 'completed recently' on Thorny Mountain, built by CCC labor. The story does not use either item. The editor should decide whether the 1935 date, the 'not confirmed' sentence, or the height note needs them. Staffing not recorded: the NHLR shows 'Staffed? No' but the quote is split across lines. Six page reads used. No photos recorded. Elevation on the NHLR page is 3,385 ft (1,032 m), consistent with the brief.

Closure and access are well supported by the 2025 news report, which is a Wyoming News Exchange piece; the Forest Service order itself was not read. Build year is disputed (1939 vs. completion October 1940). Elevation differs between NHLR (9,383 ft) and firelookout.com (9492'). The 2014 report says Historic Core; the 2025 article says HistoriCorps; the story treats them as the same group but that is not confirmed. Not read: Living New Deal (403 error), a Sheridan Press closure article and a 2024 Cowboy State Daily piece (search snippets only). No last-watch date found; the 1980 end date comes from the 2025 article. No photos added; NHLR photo credits not checked.

Thin on history: only three pages read and no fire or rental record found. Do not confuse with the Bighorn Mountains Black Mountain (Sheridan County, BHNF, built 1939 by the CCC, now boarded up); the Sheridan travel-history article and the Road Trip Ryan page describe that tower. Staffing dates in the register come from the 2018 visit and may have changed. Personal names of past lookouts are kept to the published lists.

No source checked actually states a 1950 build year for the current tower; both NHLR and Recreation.gov agree on 1963, so the earlier draft's claimed 1950/1963 discrepancy was unsupported and has been removed. No clear record of when active staffing ended beyond NHLR's '25 years then standby' note, and no date given for when that standby period began.

Build year 1941 rests on the register alone; the KINGFM CCC attribution is a hiking video's narration quoted second-hand and is unverified. The 'standing' status comes from the firelookout.org index, not the register text. The access level 'public' is inferred from the hiking account, not stated by any source. Brief record checked: name, county, elevation, agency and 2022 registration match the register, so no corrections. Not reached: Bridger-Teton lookout records or a Forest Service page on current status; a 2022 Wyoming fire report mentioning the Cabin Creek lookout cabin appeared in search but was not read. The story does not claim a current site check.

Could not fetch the bhpioneer.com newspaper article (HTTP 429, too many requests) within the read budget, so staffing/anecdote detail rests on NHLR and the brochure PDF plus firelookout.com's personnel list; worth a retry later for any additional staffing or incident detail. Did not verify current rental/public-access specifics (e.g. whether the tower cab itself is open to visitors) beyond the brief's existing 'public' access level. 2026-10-04 fact-check: the story originally said the lookout straddles the Wyoming-South Dakota line; no source supports that, and firelookout.com (source 2) instead places it in Crook County, Wyoming, about a mile from the state line. Fixed the story wording and citation accordingly.

Height_m taken from Wikipedia's 26.25 ft (8.00 m) structure height, not from ground elevation. Material conflict (wood vs concrete) flagged but not independently resolved beyond preferring the NRHP-sourced Wikipedia account.

Build date is disputed: NHLR circa 1940; county page and brochure 1941 (CCC role claimed on the county page, possible but undocumented per the brochure). The brochure says the cab was moved from Red Castles on Bare Pass before 1955, which the NHLR record does not mention. Restoration start: August 2015 (Pinedale) vs 2016-2019 (brochure). Unread leads: a 2020 Pinedale Online piece says built around 1941 by the CCC; a search snippet from npshistory.com (Lookouts, Latrines, and Lodgepole Cabins, hcs-2.pdf) says the lookout is recommended not eligible for the National Register; neither was read or verified. Road access is from a 2019 brochure; check current conditions with the Big Piney Ranger District before publishing visit advice.

The 1941 build year is supported by the register, firelookout.com and a 1941 newspaper item reprinted on West Lookouts, which is a secondary transcription. The 1940 telephone-line item calls the site a fire lookout before the 1941 build report; I could not settle whether an earlier structure stood there. The abandonment claim comes from a hiking listing, not an agency record. No staffing, fire or current access source was found, so none is stated. Brief record checked: the name, elevation, agency and 2022 registration match, so no corrections were needed. Not reached: Bridger-Teton or Bridger NF lookout records, and the NHLR nomination file for WY 21.

Build year 1938 is supported by three sources, but a 1942 newspaper item (quoted on westlookouts) calls Huckleberry a permanent station that year; not resolved. Current status is unconfirmed: the newest dated text read is the register entry (2011 registration; 'slated for restoration') and firelookout.com 'Standing'. Elevation conflict (7,209 ft register vs 9,615 ft nomination and firelookout) is proposed as a correction for human review. Page budget was used up before reading the Wyoming SHPO page, the Jackson Hole Mountain Resort page or the Hiking Project page; search snippets claim restoration and overnight use, but those were not read or cited, so check them before any access statement is changed. No new photos.

Elevation conflict left unresolved: register 9,395 ft (2,864 m, matches the record's 2863.6 m) vs Forest Service 9,477 ft. NRHP listing date: register says December 2016, Wikipedia says November 15, 2016. Footprint: register and Wikipedia give 14 ft square, the nomination gives a 20 ft exterior footprint. The Forest Service page spells the name 'James Torrey Saban'; the register says 'James T.', so the story keeps 'James T.' and does not expand it. Current staffing and access come from the Forest Service page (last updated May 13, 2025), not a site visit. A search snippet about an overnight rental concerned Sheep Mountain, a different lookout, and was not used. The nomination gives no date for the restoration work. No new photos.

The brief's 1969 build date is contradicted by three sources (1964); Wilma Perue's 1969-1971 tenure may be the source of the mix-up. Rental fee comes from a Forest Service page last updated June 6, 2025; confirm before publishing. The record's kind 'two_story' is not supported by any source read: the NHLR describes a single R-6 cab with an interpretive site on a lower level. No fire or move history found; the CCC-era cab is undated beyond the 1930s.

Built year and register data are well sourced. The 1926 build date (Outside Bozeman) is unresolved and reported as a conflict. Jim McCown (1963-1987) rests on one listing and is not confirmed; the 1975 visitor's Jim is unnamed, so the story does not link them. Current condition is inferred from a standing listing and a photo caption; no recent condition report was read. A search summary attributed a 1991 removal to this lookout, but the Outside Bozeman article's 1991 removal concerns Divide Lookout, not Sheridan, so it is not used. Blueprint location conflicts: WillhiteWeb says the Montana State Library holds them; Montana History Portal item 93097 credits the Yellowstone National Park Heritage and Research Center. Access level is unknown; no source read says whether the cabin can be entered. Height is not stated in any source; elevation_m is from the register. The record's Park County is supported; the Teton County listing is the only conflict.

Build date is contested: the NHLR Built field and HABS say 1941, but the NHLR narrative says construction began June 1939 and was completed summer 1940. The record keeps 1941; the story reports both. The 1921 stone lookout (Willhite, HABS, NHLR) is treated as the predecessor. The NPS page is undated; its staffing statement is in the present tense. Drive-up status rests on HABS (a parking area north of the building; the lookout described as the only Yellowstone fire lookout facility accessible by vehicle) plus two NPS hiking trails. Road seasonality and whether the upper floors are open to visitors were not checked. No fire events beyond the staffing history and the 1980 modification appear in the sources read. No climbing advice is given.

Build year (1941) and staffing are consistent across NHLR and the 1941 newspaper items as transcribed on Forest Lookouts; the original newspaper scans were not read. Current access, rental status and condition are not established beyond the July 2025 FFLA post. A June 2025 Pinedale Online / geolconsulting article on protecting the tower could not be read (SSL certificate errors from both fetch_text and WebFetch), so the wrap and fire details rest on the FFLA post alone. Elevation differs between NHLR (9,665 ft) and firelookout.com (9642'). Access is omitted because no level could be supported. No photos added.

A travel-blog page (roadtripryan.com) and the WebSearch AI summary both offered a vivid, specific narrative - an 1922 primitive fire watch predecessor and a 1938 lightning strike that set the lookout's bed on fire - that appears nowhere in the NHLR register, the FFLA register, or the Forest Service's own Bighorn lookouts history page. I did not use any of that material; it has the hallmarks of AI-generated filler rather than sourced history, and a human may want to track down the roadtripryan.com page's own citations if any exist. Note that the CCC-construction claim itself is NOT part of that invented narrative - Recreation.gov and the Rocket-Miner newspaper piece (sources 4 and 6, both used in the story) independently and directly state the lookout was 'Constructed in 1950 by the Civilian Conservation Corps,' so that part is sourced, just flagged in the story as doubtful because the CCC was disbanded in 1942. A footnote error was also fixed: the story had attributed the 'Emergency' staffing status to 'the Forest Fire Lookout Association's own register,' but that fact actually comes from firelookout.com, an independent reference site by Rex Kamstra, not from FFLA's own site (firelookout.org, source 3) - the FFLA page for Wyoming is just a name/county/status table with no staffing field for this lookout. Text corrected; footnote [^2] was already pointing at the right source. The record's elevation_m (2911.8m / ~9554ft) runs a little low against the 9600-9610ft the registers give; likely just rounding/survey differences, not flagged as a correction. No other conflicts found worth a formal correction.

No new photos found beyond those already on the tower record. The exact abandonment year is unknown (NHLR hedges with 'most probably ... mid to late 1940's'); I used 1945 as a placeholder year for the 'abandoned' event rather than inventing precision. The kind correction (tower -> shelter) is worth a human look since 'tower' vs 'shelter' is partly a classification judgment, not a hard fact.

Height_m in the record (9.1 m / ~30 ft) likely describes the original 1930s pole tower rather than the current 41-55 ft structure; worth checking against a primary USFS record before correcting. Exact year of the tower replacement (after the original 1938 build) is not pinned down by any source consulted.

History is well sourced across the Forest Service, NHLR and Wikipedia. Access and restroom details rest on Hiking Project, a third-party listing that may be out of date. The brief's design L-4 most likely describes the 1938 cab, so it is corrected. The first lookout's name is unresolved: NHLR says Mert Ellsbury, firelookout.com says Lyman Ellsbury for 1939. The story reports both. Staffing source is NHLR undated text, so as_of is undated. Brief elevation 2028.7 m matches NHLR 6,656 ft; Wikipedia says 6,640 ft. Sundance AFS radar claim is from the Forest Service page and was not separately checked. No photos added.

Status is likely wrong in the tower record (see correction) and should be fixed by an editor, not auto-applied. Build year is fuzzy (1932 vs. ~1934) because NHLR's stated span and the Buckrail piece's '23 years of service ending 1957' don't quite agree; left unresolved rather than guessed. No NRHP nomination form or newspaper coverage was found for this one — the two non-register sources (firelookout.com, Buckrail) carried the real narrative detail (staff names, prior tent/stone camp). Fact-check correction (2026-10-04): a draft version of the story attributed a 2000 near-miss wildfire to Wyoming Peak, citing the Buckrail article; that passage in Buckrail is actually about Deadman Fire Lookout, a different lookout covered in the same article, and has been removed.

research_corrections.name: Evergreen Mountain Lookout
research_corrections.current: Rental description (sourced from Recreation.gov/ridb) states the lookout was placed on the NRHP during 1990s volunteer restoration; willhiteweb.com independently repeats the same claim.
research_corrections.proposed: NPGallery's own NRHP asset record gives a listing date of July 14, 1987, a decade before the restoration effort described on Recreation.gov and willhiteweb.com. The two popular accounts agree with each other but disagree with the primary NRHP record; this should be reconciled or flagged in the record.
research_corrections.evidence: NPGallery AssetDetail page for NRIS 87001187 states a listing date of July 14, 1987 as part of a multiple-property submission; Recreation.gov's description ('During volunteer restoration efforts in the 1990s, the lookout was placed on the National Register of Historic Places') and willhiteweb.com ('During restoration it was placed on the National Register of Historic Places') both attribute the listing to the 1990s restoration instead.
